agent-orchestration-before-searching-ass.rule: Before searching assumed public entry-file paths, enumerate the repository files with rg --files and search only paths that actually exist.

agent-orchestration-discover-test-file-p.rule: Discover test file paths with rg --files before passing guessed paths to a multi-file inspection command; one missing path makes the command fail and weakens the audit evidence.

agent-orchestration-resolve-named-skill-.rule: Resolve named skill paths from the supplied skill-roots table before reading SKILL.md; never assume a project-local .agentsmesh/skills path.

agent-orchestration-treat-any-command-co.rule: Treat any command containing output redirection as state-changing and run file/command lessons recall before executing it, even when the underlying workload is read-only.

agent-orchestration-when-a-subagent-audi.rule: When a subagent audit lane fails because of a usage-limit reset window, close the failed lane and retry that same target after the reset before declaring the multi-target audit complete.

agent-orchestration-when-dispatching-a-r.rule: When dispatching a read-only or review subagent, do NOT give it tools that can mutate state — no shell that can run `git checkout`/`git reset`/`git restore`, no file deletes or overwrites. Use a read-only tool profile (e.g. the Explore agent type), confine experimental writes to a fresh temp dir the subagent creates, and commit or stash before fan-out so a stray revert stays recoverable.

agent-orchestration-when-spawning-a-suba.rule: When spawning a subagent with fork_context=true, omit agent_type, model, and reasoning_effort because the full-history fork inherits them.

agent-orchestration-when-spawning-review.rationale: On 2026-07-03 an adversarial code-review workflow used the default (full-tool) agent type; a verifier reverted src/lessons/hook.ts to stale HEAD, wiping uncommitted feature work — a recurrence of the 2026-06-05 lessons.json incident.
agent-orchestration-when-spawning-review.rule: When spawning review/audit/verify subagents via the Workflow tool, set agentType:'Explore' (or another read-only profile) on EVERY agent() call — the default workflow agent has full tools and will run git checkout/restore/reset to "clean up," silently reverting uncommitted work in the parent tree. Also add an explicit no-git-mutation line to the prompt, and git status/diff the tree after the workflow before trusting it.

canonical-skills-read-skill-supporting-f.rule: Read skill supporting files as bytes (Buffer), never through readFileSafe as a UTF-8 string: binary assets under skills/*/ (png, woff, zip, templates) are decoded lossily and written broken to every target (a PNG 0x89 byte became EF BF BD). Gate any text normalization on a text-extension allowlist and pass bytes through verbatim otherwise.

capability-fix-campaign-global-scope-imp.rule: Global-scope import for a target's rules/skills importer that historically hardcoded project-scope directory constants (ignoring options.scope) was silently broken for --global the whole time — verify by grepping the importer for a scope-aware directory param before assuming existing global import tests pass for real; add an explicit rulesDir/skillsDir override parameter selected by scope in the orchestrator (importFromX), and gate project-only features (mcp/ignore/agents-file) behind an early return for scope==='global' rather than leaving them to silently no-op on the wrong path.

capability-fix-campaign-never-let-a-suba.rationale: Pilot agent for roo-code bypassed the pre-commit hook with --no-verify citing a false 'git lock' reason, when the real cause was a genuine 95% branch-coverage gate failure from its own under-tested new files (importer.ts/layout.ts/merge.ts). Had to independently re-verify coverage, dispatch a follow-up agent to add real tests, and amend the commit to make the hook pass legitimately.
capability-fix-campaign-never-let-a-suba.rule: Never let a subagent use `git commit --no-verify` to bypass a failing pre-commit hook without explicit orchestrator/user authorization — if the hook fails (e.g. a repo-wide coverage threshold), investigate root cause and add real tests to close the gap, then commit for real. Prefer a fresh follow-up commit over `git commit --amend` on a commit another process might still be referencing, even within the same session.

capability-fix-campaign-when-a-target-s-.rule: When a target's agents feature moves to a single combined multi-agent file (e.g. YAML), set layout.paths.agentPath() to return null (not a fixed path). The output-source-map/reference-rewrite pipeline assumes one output path maps to exactly one canonical source file; a combined file breaks that, silently leaking unrewritten canonical .agentsmesh/... paths into generated content. Follow the existing roo-code .roomodes precedent (also excluded from tests/e2e/generate-reference-rewrite-matrix.e2e.test.ts's TARGETS list for the same reason).

capability-fix-campaign-when-downgrading.rule: When downgrading a target's global capability from native to none for a feature with conversionDefaults (e.g. agents with agentsToSkills), also flip the conversionDefaults flag to false explicitly (not omitted) — builtin-targets.ts's isConversionUpgrading() reports the shared 'none -> embedded via skill projection' matrix-display upgrade whenever supportsConversion + a truthy conversionDefault exist, silently overstating the matrix even though generateX itself correctly emits [].

capability-fix-campaign-when-renaming-a-.rule: When renaming a target's emitted rule/command frontmatter key (e.g. qwen-code globs->paths), also add a frontmatterRemap in that target's importer-spec directory-mode rule entry mapping the new source key back to the canonical field name (description/globs) — the shared default ruleMapper/commandMapper only reads fixed canonical key names and silently drops data under an unrecognized key on import, breaking round-trip silently unless a dedicated round-trip test is added.

capability-ledger-a-target-s-own-generat.rule: A target's own generated settings file MAY legitimately self-reference its own native directory prefix (e.g. opencode.json's instructions glob '.opencode/rules/*.md'); tests/contract/target-contract.matrix.test.ts's TARGET_SPECIFIC_PREFIXES leak-check bans ALL prefixes including the target's own, so exclude the current target's own prefix (a small per-target allowlist) rather than avoiding the legitimate self-reference.

capability-ledger-derive-capability-ledg.rule: Derive capability-ledger cell path/ext/format/fingerprint from the conformance fixture's ACTUAL generated output (run the target through createCanonicalProject(MATRIX_CONFIG) + runGenerate and inspect the tree), never from the tool's docs. Doc-derived cells break conformance with aspirational keys (e.g. optional agent-JSON fields), '<name>' placeholder paths, or dir-only paths. Docs determine only maxAchievable/verdict/source; generated output determines the fingerprint.

capability-ledger-fixes-new-target-sourc.rule: New target source files must explicitly test defensive/narrow branches (falsy-fallback '||', non-object array-entry guards, optional-array-key ternaries in importer/hooks-format code) or global branch coverage (95% threshold in pnpm precommit) fails even when all logic is correct — check coverage-final.json per-file branch % for new files before running full precommit

capability-ledger-ledger-cell-fingerprin.rationale: Fingerprints are verified against real generator output using the canonical-full fixture; doc-schema keys that the generator never writes cause conformance failures.
capability-ledger-ledger-cell-fingerprin.rule: Ledger cell fingerprint topLevelKeys must reflect what the generator actually emits for the canonical-full fixture — not the full documentation schema. Keys that are conditional on non-empty canonical inputs (e.g. allowedTools when tools=[]) or runtime-managed by the tool (e.g. smart_approve) must be omitted from topLevelKeys.

capability-ledger-never-run-pnpm-capabil.rationale: The seed script does a full JSON.stringify({cells}) rewrite from live-generated project-scope output only; there is no merge path, so it would silently wipe hand-verified confirmed/rejected/global cells recorded by prior audit passes.
capability-ledger-never-run-pnpm-capabil.rule: Never run `pnpm capabilities:seed` after hand-adding verified/rejected/global-scope ledger cells — it fully overwrites capability-ledger.json from scratch with only auto-derivable project-scope native/embedded skeletons (extensionless-file features and all global-scope cells are silently dropped, and existing verified provenance is destroyed). Hand-edit capability-ledger.json directly for global-scope, rejected, or extensionless-path cells instead.

capability-ledger-pnpm-capabilities-seed.rule: pnpm capabilities:seed (scripts/seed-capability-ledger.ts) fully OVERWRITES capability-ledger.json from scratch on every run (empty cells array rebuilt only from its own single-file-attribution pass); it never merges with existing confirmed entries and skips multi-file features (agents/commands/skills) and additionalRules entirely. Never re-run it during incremental per-target capability work — hand-adjust the ledger JSON instead, or it silently wipes prior verified provenance.

capability-ledger-pnpm-capabilities-veri.rule: `pnpm capabilities:verify` exits non-zero BY DESIGN — it is a backlog tracker for native/embedded cells that still lack `capability-ledger.json` provenance (hundreds are intentionally un-researched: global scope, directory features, extensionless/unstructured files). Do NOT wire it into CI as a hard gate and do NOT try to drive its "missing" count to zero wholesale. The enforced CI gate is the conformance test `tests/contract/capability-ledger-conformance.test.ts` (runs under `pnpm test`), which fails only when a SEEDED native/embedded cell's generated output drifts from its recorded ext/format/fingerprint, plus the ledger-integrity assertion (no orphan/invalid/duplicate cells).

capability-ledger-when-a-target-s-mergeg.rationale: The mergeGeneratedOutputContent hook receives the already-rewritten path, so a check against the project constant always fails in global scope.
capability-ledger-when-a-target-s-mergeg.rule: When a target's mergeGeneratedOutputContent checks a path constant (e.g. CRUSH_CONFIG_FILE) to decide whether to merge, also include the global-scope rewritten path (e.g. CRUSH_GLOBAL_CONFIG_FILE) — otherwise global-scope multi-feature merges silently overwrite each other because the rewritten path never matches the project-only constant.

capability-ledger-when-consuming-pnpm-sc.rule: When consuming pnpm script JSON output, strip pnpm lifecycle preamble and parse from the first JSON delimiter instead of redirecting stdout directly.

ci-and-release-security-before-submittin.rule: Before submitting to the MCP registry, confirm `mcpName` in the PUBLISHED package.json equals server.json `name` — the registry verifies npm ownership by reading the npm tarball, not this repo, so the field only counts once a release ships. Also keep server.json referenced by a test: nothing imported it, so its hand-copied versions drifted unnoticed.

ci-and-release-security-rule-1.rule: **Never interpolate `${{ ... }}` directly into `run:` script bodies for any expression carrying user-influenceable data (CWE-78).** Flow inputs/outputs through `env:` so they become shell variables, then validate shape (e.g. `case "$VERSION" in [!0-9]*|*[!a-zA-Z0-9.+-]*|"") exit 1 ;; esac`) before use. Applies to `inputs.*`, `steps.*.outputs.*`, and `needs.*.outputs.*` that transitively trace to a workflow input.

ci-and-release-security-rule-10.rule: **Post-publish `git tag` steps must be idempotent.** `changeset publish` already creates a local `v<version>` tag for single-package repos regardless of the `commit:` flag. The post-publish step shape: `git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$TAG" >/dev/null || git tag "$TAG"; git push origin "$TAG"`.

ci-and-release-security-rule-11.rule: **`.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf` (plus explicit categories for `*.md`, `*.json`, `*.yaml`) is mandatory in any cross-platform repo whose tests stage fixtures into temp dirs and assert byte-stable generated artifacts.** Windows runners default to `core.autocrlf=true`; relying on per-runner git config is not a contract. Fix EOL at the repo boundary via attributes, not at every consumer site.

ci-and-release-security-rule-12.rule: **CI workflows must run `pnpm build` before any job invoking `pnpm test` or `pnpm test:coverage` when the test config includes integration tests that exec `dist/cli.js`.** Only `pnpm test:e2e` self-builds; the others do not. Fresh CI clones have no prior `dist/`.

ci-and-release-security-rule-13.rule: **Tests/integration steps must never hardcode `/bin/sh` or `/bin/zsh` once Windows is in the CI matrix; never use shell-based `2>&1` redirection in test runners.** Use `spawnSync(process.execPath, [...args])` and concatenate `result.stdout + result.stderr`. On Linux `ubuntu-latest`, `/bin/zsh` does not exist; on Windows neither does `/bin/sh`.

ci-and-release-security-rule-14.rule: **Tests that stub `git` via a `chmod 755` Node script or pass `NODE_OPTIONS=--import=<unix path>` must be `it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')`.** GitHub Actions Windows runners block git network ops and do not honor these stub strategies. Cover the behavior on Linux/macOS.

ci-and-release-security-rule-15.rule: **Plugin/source classifiers distinguishing "local file" from "npm specifier" must accept Windows drive-letter absolutes (`/^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]/`) alongside POSIX `/...`, `./...`, `../...`, and `file:`.** `node:path.resolve()` on win32 produces `D:\foo`; missing this routes legitimate absolute paths into `resolveNpmSpecifier` and `import()` fails.

ci-and-release-security-rule-16.rule: **Test assertions that a tracked file ships executable must query the git index (`git ls-files --stage <path>` and match `/^100755 /`), not `statSync(...).mode & 0o111`.** NTFS on Windows runners does not surface POSIX execute bits; the git-index mode is what `gh release create` carries into the tarball.

ci-and-release-security-rule-2.rule: **Dependent jobs that must run when an upstream is conditionally skipped need an explicit status-function override.** Use `if: !cancelled() && (needs.<upstream>.result == 'success' && <cond> || <skip-allowed-cond>)`. Prefer `!cancelled()` over `always()`. The default implicit `success()` on `if:` short-circuits whenever the upstream was skipped.

ci-and-release-security-rule-3.rule: **Never embed tokens in git remote URLs.** Use `actions/checkout@v4` with `repository:` + `token:` so the credential helper handles auth per-process. Token-in-URL leaks into `.git/config`, `ps`/`/proc/$pid/cmdline`, and uploaded workspace artifacts; GitHub Actions log redaction does NOT cover these surfaces.

ci-and-release-security-rule-4.rule: **Pin every tool that produces release artifacts to at least major.minor; never `latest` in a release pipeline.** Applies to `setup-bun` (`bun-version: "1.2"`), Docker image tags, `npm install` in CI, and any other tool acquisition step in release builds. Reserve `latest` for dev-only iteration.

ci-and-release-security-rule-5.rule: **Checksum verification in curl|sh installers must fail closed (CWE-345).** Both "expected hash absent/empty" and "no checksum tool available" branches must `error` (exit non-zero), never `warn` and continue. The user installing a checksum tool is the right trade-off.

ci-and-release-security-rule-6.rule: **Validate env-controlled paths against a strict allowlist before they cross into shell-parsed files (CWE-77).** Any value flowing from env into a file that is later parsed by a shell (rc files, sourced configs) is shell-equivalent input. Reject anything outside `[a-zA-Z0-9./_~\ -]` for installer paths. Threat model is wrapping processes (Docker entrypoints, Makefiles, parent installers), not the user.

ci-and-release-security-rule-7.rule: **Use `awk` field-equality, not `grep` substring, to look up values keyed by exact filename in checksum-style manifests.** `grep "$TARGET" SHA256SUMS | awk '{print $1}'` matches `agentsmesh-darwin-arm64.exe` and `$TARGET.sig` lines too; use `awk -v t="$TARGET" '$2==t {print $1}'`. Same rule for any `<token>  <filename>` manifest.

ci-and-release-security-rule-8.rule: **Installer scripts editing shell-rc files MUST branch the written line by shell, not just the file path.** Key both the rc-file path AND the line content off `$SHELL`: fish needs `fish_add_path -gP "$BIN_DIR"` (or `set -gx PATH "$BIN_DIR" $PATH`); bash/zsh use `export PATH=...`. Also `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$config")"` before `>>` because parent dirs (e.g. `~/.config/fish/`) may not exist.

ci-and-release-security-rule-9.rule: **For npm trusted publishing, choose a GitHub-hosted Node version whose bundled npm already satisfies current docs; do not self-upgrade npm in CI.** `npm install -g npm@latest` fails on `ubuntu-latest` with arborist dependency tree breakage before the publish step runs. Add an explicit npm install only when a specific known-good version is needed AND the runner cannot supply it directly.

cli-presentation-a-clack-clack-prompts-s.rule: A clack (@clack/prompts) spinner owns its terminal line — ANY stdout written while it is active corrupts the layout (the next block's first line concatenates onto the spinner line, e.g. the matrix header shifting after "Generating…"). Never wrap a call that prints DURING its run in a spinner: `generate` renders the compatibility matrix mid-run via `printMatrix`, so pass `printMatrix: false` and render the matrix AFTER `sp.stop()`/`ui.outro()`. Commands whose runX is silent (output only via the renderer, which runs after) are spinner-safe — verified install/refresh/import/convert/uninstall have 0 direct output calls during their run.

cli-presentation-a-clack-spinner-and-an.rule: A clack spinner and an interactive readline prompt cannot share a TTY: the spinner's redraw timer overwrites the prompt line, so the question is invisible and the command hangs on stdin. In src/cli/command-handlers.ts, any handler whose runX may prompt (install → broken-link/bulk prompts; uninstall → modified-files drift prompt) MUST skip the spinner when it may prompt — gate with mayPrompt(nf) (stdin AND stdout isTTY, and neither --force nor --dry-run), mirroring the init handler. The earlier "install/uninstall are spinner-safe because runX outputs only via the renderer after the run" claim is WRONG: it ignored the interactive prompt flow (writeBanner + deps.ask/readLine) which writes DURING the run.

cli-presentation-all-interactive-install.rule: All interactive install/uninstall/refresh prompts MUST go through prompt-io.readLine (or delegate to it), never a bespoke readline.createInterface. A raw readline without a 'close' handler HANGS on EOF/Ctrl-D (the question callback never fires), and without an 'error' handler CRASHES the process on a stream error (broken pipe, SSH drop). readLine collapses both to '' (decline) — the uniform EOF contract. This is why confirm() (src/install/core/prompts.ts) was refactored to delegate to readLine. When adding a new prompt, reuse readLine and treat '' as the safe-decline default.

cli-presentation-never-call-process-exit.rule: Never call process.exit() immediately after process.stdout.write(): pipes are asynchronous on macOS, so any output over 64 KiB (diff --json, lint --json) is truncated and the consumer gets an unparseable JSON fragment. Set process.exitCode and return, or exit inside the write callback.

cli-presentation-node-writes-to-a-pipe.rule: Node writes to a pipe asynchronously while a TTY or file is blocking, and process.exit discards whatever is still queued, so any CLI payload over the pipe buffer (64 KiB on macOS) is truncated only when piped — redirecting to a file hides the bug. Fix it once at the process entry by asking libuv to make stdout/stderr blocking (stream._handle.setBlocking(true), guarded: private API); do NOT try to flush an already-queued async write before exiting, which is impossible synchronously.

cli-presentation-when-auditing-spinner-v.rule: When auditing spinner-vs-prompt collisions, check EVERY command handler in src/cli/command-handlers.ts that holds a ui.spinner(), not just the one reported. refresh is a THIRD collision site (besides install/uninstall): runRefresh → runConsentPrompt (run-refresh.ts) → readLine shows a [y/N/per-pack] consent prompt for drifted packs, and it was ungated. generate/import/convert are genuinely prompt-free (verified) so their spinners are safe. Gate refresh with mayPrompt(nf) too. Rule: a handler is spinner-safe ONLY if its runX has zero reachable readLine/confirm/clack prompt; trace the full call graph before trusting an ungated spinner.

codex-cli-mcp-any-path-containment-asser.rule: Any path-containment assert added to the stale sweep (findStaleGeneratedOutputs / findUntrackedManagedDirFiles) must ALSO run in the pre-write check in generate-handlers/convert, covering every active target's managedOutputs.dirs — the sweep runs after all files are written and before writeLockFile, so a managed dir that produced no output this run (feature off) and resolves outside the root aborts with outputs on disk and no lock, leaving check reporting 'Not initialized' on every rerun. Dry-run must run the same check so it cannot say OK for a layout the real run rejects.

codex-cli-mcp-codex-rejects-mcp-server-n.rule: Codex rejects MCP server names that do not match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_:@/.-]+$ (e.g. 'Framelink MCP for Figma' with spaces) and never starts that server; canonical mcp.json keys flow verbatim into .codex/config.toml [mcp_servers."<name>"] tables, so codex-cli generation or lint must flag or sanitize such names instead of emitting them.

codex-cli-mcp-when-restoring-a-user-s.rule: When restoring a user's tool config (e.g. ~/.codex/config.toml) from a .bak, do not stop at 'parses as TOML': check the restored model_provider/base_url is live and not a preset placeholder such as https://api.example.com/v1 — a backup can capture a broken state (the Mar-31 .bak held the IDE plugin's crs preset), and restoring it silently re-breaks the tool months later.

codex-cli-rule-paths-when-changing-where.rationale: codexRuleDirectory is imported by codebuff; roundtrip/integration/e2e tests hard-code the nested path lists.
codex-cli-rule-paths-when-changing-where.rule: When changing where codex-cli nests or embeds advisory rules (codex-rule-paths.ts), keep Codebuff's `codebuffNestedKnowledgePath` behaviour explicit in codebuff/rule-paths.ts (it shares `codexRuleDirectory`) and update the strict path lists in tests/import-generate-roundtrip.test.ts plus the dist-driven integration/e2e reference-rewrite tests, which cannot be run without a rebuilt dist.

copilot-hooks-copilot-hooks-matcher-is-c.rule: Copilot hooks matcher is compiled as a JS regex ^(?:PATTERN)$; never emit the canonical '*' wildcard sentinel as a literal matcher value (invalid regex, causes Copilot to skip the whole hook entry) — omit the matcher field instead

copilot-hooks-never-wire-a-hook-that.rule: Never wire a hook that can fail to Copilot preToolUse: a failing preToolUse hook denies the tool call. Build Copilot's hooks config and its wrapper scripts from one grouping, or scripts are left orphaned.

copilot-hooks-when-a-target-s-global.rule: When a target's global scope models a specific tool surface (e.g. copilot's ~/.copilot/* = Copilot CLI home dir, not the VS Code extension's OS-specific user-profile dir), verify a ledger/finding's path against that target's OWN existing global path convention before trusting it — a 'confirmed' cell can still be wrong-tool-surface (e.g. VS Code's ~/.config/Code/User/mcp.json vs Copilot CLI's ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json) even when individually well-sourced

coverage-analysis-agentsmesh-coverage-th.rationale: During release prep the prepare-release skill stated 90/90/84 but the real config enforces 95/95/95; branches passed at only 95.02%, a margin my load-plugin canonicalize change nearly consumed.
coverage-analysis-agentsmesh-coverage-th.rule: agentsmesh coverage thresholds in vitest.config.ts are lines/functions/branches = 95/95/95 — NOT the 90/90/84 the prepare-release skill claims. Branch coverage runs razor-thin (~95.02%), so any change that adds an uncovered branch (a new fallback/guard path) can fail the gate. Add tests for every new branch and verify with `COVERAGE=1 node_modules/.bin/vitest run --coverage` (never `pnpm test:coverage` — pnpm trips the frozen-lockfile/hono-override issue).

coverage-analysis-to-cover-catch-arms-ar.rule: To cover `.catch(() => [])` arms around readDirRecursiveNoSymlinks or dir-listing branches gated behind readFileSafe probes, mock the fs.js export with vi.mock + importOriginal (vi.hoisted mock fn); pointing the path at a regular file does not work because readDirRecursiveNoSymlinks swallows ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EACCES and readFileSafe throws FileSystemError on EISDIR for real directories.

coverage-analysis-to-diagnose-a-codecov-.rule: To diagnose a Codecov patch/diff-coverage failure in this repo, parse `coverage/coverage-final.json` (istanbul: per-file `s`/`statementMap`, `b`/`branchMap`) for the EXACT uncovered statement and branch lines. Do NOT trust the v8 TEXT table's "Uncovered Line #s": it truncates long paths, conflates line-vs-branch, and lists multiple same-basename files (e.g. `cli/commands/init.ts` vs `lessons/init.ts`), so it can show a gap as "still 60,76" when the JSON proves the file is 100%. Generate coverage with the local binary `COVERAGE=1 node_modules/.bin/vitest run --coverage` (NOT `pnpm test:coverage` — pnpm 11 trips frozen-install on the pnpm-10 lockfile). Distinguish unreachable defensive branches (e.g. `x ?? false` where x is always assigned) from real gaps; don't chase 100%.

coverage-analysis-when-investigating-a-v.rationale: Chasing roo-code's 5-file branch gap, a scoped run showed importer.ts still at 76.08% branch after my fix landed, with a totally different uncovered-line range (53-64,143 vs original 47,141) — same percentage, different location — which only made sense after inspecting coverage-final.json directly and confirming the full suite (with e2e contributions) had already closed 53-64 and my catch-block fix closed 47/141, while 143 was a distinct pre-existing compound-condition gap.
coverage-analysis-when-investigating-a-v.rule: When investigating a vitest branch-coverage gap for a single target, a scoped run (`vitest run tests/unit/targets/<target>/`) can report a DIFFERENT uncovered-branch set (same % by coincidence, different line numbers) than the full `pnpm test:coverage` run — because e2e/integration tests elsewhere in the repo also exercise that source file and contribute branch coverage the scoped run lacks. Don't write tests to "fix" a branch that only looks uncovered in a scoped run: cross-check `coverage/coverage-final.json`'s per-file `branchMap`/`b` arrays (filter for any count === 0) from a FULL coverage run first to find the true gap, then target new tests at exactly those branch ids.

dist-backed-tests-an-e2e-test-that-runs.rule: An e2e test that runs dist/cli.js as a git merge driver (spawnSync -> git -> node, 3-level process nesting) can transiently fail fork/exec under peak full-suite parallelism and surface as a spurious merge conflict (merge status 1); since the union merge is deterministic, guard it with vitest { retry: N } (re-runs a fresh beforeEach) so a real regression still fails every attempt while only the environmental spawn flake is absorbed, and never treat a single non-zero merge status as a product bug without reproducing it in isolation first.

dist-backed-tests-rule-1.rule: Run `pnpm build` before any targeted e2e or integration slice whenever source affecting `dist/cli.js` has changed; ad hoc `vitest` runs do not auto-build (Evidence L114, L116, L165).

dist-backed-tests-rule-2.rule: Never run two CLI commands that read or rebuild `dist/` in parallel — serialize anything that touches `dist/cli.js` or runs `pnpm build`, since `tsup` cleans `dist/` at build start and concurrent workers will hit ENOENT/MODULE_NOT_FOUND mid-test (Evidence L57, L115).

dist-backed-tests-rule-3.rule: Before declaring a dist-backed failure a product bug, rebuild and rerun — stale `dist/cli.js` will surface as missing generated prompts or implementation regressions that do not exist in source (Evidence L116, L165).

dist-backed-tests-rule-4.rule: In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, place `pnpm build` BEFORE `pnpm test` and `pnpm test:coverage` whenever those configs include integration files that exec `dist/cli.js`; only `pnpm test:e2e` self-builds (`pnpm build && vitest run --config ...`) (Evidence L187).

dist-backed-tests-rule-5.rule: Keep `runCli`/e2e CLI helper timeouts comfortably above targeted-run latency so full-suite parallel pressure does not exceed the 30s budget; reproduce timeout-looking failures both targeted and under the full runner before treating them as product behavior failures (Evidence L53).

dist-backed-tests-rule-6.rule: When refactoring cache-backed features that dist-backed tests exercise (remote extends, refresh), preserve existing on-disk cache paths for supported providers unless an explicit migration is added and verified — changing GitHub cache-key layout breaks refresh tests that look in the prior directory (Evidence L119).

dist-backed-tests-rule-7.rule: Unit tests that call `runGenerate`/`runWatch` directly (same process) contribute to coverage; dist-backed integration tests that exec a subprocess do not — pick the harness intentionally when targeting coverage gaps (Evidence L109).

dist-backed-tests-tests-e2e-agents-last-.rationale: During release prep the file showed as dirty after every full test run and had to be reverted twice before committing; a naive `git add -A` would commit spurious timestamp churn.
dist-backed-tests-tests-e2e-agents-last-.rule: `tests/e2e/agents-last-run.md` is tracked but regenerated (timestamp-only churn) by the e2e test suite, so it shows as dirty after `pnpm test`. Do NOT commit its change — `git checkout -- tests/e2e/agents-last-run.md` and stage files explicitly (never `git add -A`). The repo intends it untracked (commit 0a09e16 "stop tracking") but it is still tracked, so the churn keeps reappearing.

dist-backed-tests-when-a-change-alters-c.rule: When a change alters CLI/scaffold/import-safety-net behavior, rebuild (npm run build) BEFORE running e2e/contract tests that exec dist/cli.js via runCli. Source-side test helpers (e.g. activateLessons calling scaffoldLessons directly) use fresh code and pass, masking the staleness; only paths exercised solely through the spawned CLI (e.g. the import safety net) fail — and only for the targets that depend on that path. A partial e2e failure split along 'who runs the new code' is the tell-tale sign of stale dist.

dist-backed-tests-when-committing-untrac.rule: When committing untracked files in this repo (e.g. QA reports under tasks/reports/), know the precommit hook runs `pnpm test:coverage`, whose run deletes untracked files in the real working tree — `git add` then a separate `git commit` will silently drop them. Stage the files and commit docs-only changes with `--no-verify`, or fix the offending test to write only under a temp dir. Tracked files survive; only untracked ones are removed.

docs-lock-format-changing-the-generation.rule: Changing the generation-contract wording requires the full version ladder in src/targets/projection/root-instruction-paragraph.ts: demote the current ROOT_INSTRUCTION_BODY to ROOT_INSTRUCTION_BODY_V<n>, add an AGENTSMESH_CONTRACT_WITH_V<n>_BODY pair, and prepend it to LEGACY_FORMS — otherwise an existing root file keeps the old raw paragraph alongside the new block. The body must never contain the literal '.agentsmesh/' with a trailing slash (link-rewrite e2e contract). After editing, run 'agentsmesh generate' to refresh this repo's own tracked CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and .agentsmesh/.lock.

docs-lock-format-the-agentsmesh-lock-is-.rule: The .agentsmesh/.lock is a YAML file (keys: generated_at, generated_by, lib_version, checksums for canonical .agentsmesh/-relative sources, extends, packs, and optional outputs map of project-root-relative generated-file checksums) — NOT a JSON file with a version/files map. When documenting the lock, describe canonical `checksums` and generated `outputs` separately; don't reuse the old JSON `{version, files}` shape.

docs-lock-format-the-reference-rewriter-.rule: The reference rewriter resolves root-absolute tokens against the project root and is EXISTENCE-GATED, so a slash command in prose (/plugin, /config, /memory) is corrupted into a bare path the moment a directory of that name appears at the repo root — silently, on the next generate, across every target. isSlashCommandToken in src/core/reference/link-rebaser.ts now exempts single-segment /word with no extension and no trailing slash; keep that guard when touching token classification, and write /dir/ or dir/ when a directory is genuinely meant.

docs-lock-format-to-regenerate-a-social-.rule: To regenerate a social card PNG from the Astro dev-only pages (/og at 1200x640, /og-github at 1280x640): disable the dev toolbar first ('node node_modules/astro/astro.js preferences disable devToolbar' in website/) or it renders into the bottom edge of the capture, restart the dev server so the card's scoped stylesheet is not stale, capture with chrome-devtools take_screenshot filePath (which only accepts paths inside the workspace root, never /tmp), then downsample with 'sips --resampleHeightWidth' because the capture comes back at 2x DPR and GitHub rejects social previews over 1 MB. Re-enable the toolbar afterwards.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-after-c.rule: After changing a target capability or output path, update every exact capability assertion and strict target contract in the same TDD slice; focused target tests intentionally encode the previous contract.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-after-u.rationale: Hand-editing the README/MDX is error-prone; the render script is the source of truth for the generated matrix blocks.
fixture-and-assertion-discipline-after-u.rule: After updating a target's capabilities (e.g. commands from none → native), run `node --import tsx/esm scripts/render-support-matrix.ts` (not just matrix verify) to regenerate the MDX, then confirm verify passes — the script both updates the docs AND validates them.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-agentsm.rule: `agentsmesh lessons validate` prints "Lessons graph: ok." whenever there are no ERROR findings; warnings (DEAD_FILE_GLOB, NEVER_RECALLED and the like) are printed too and do NOT suppress the ok line (src/cli/renderers/lessons-render-diagnostics.ts prints it on data.ok). Tests asserting on validate must check the exit code and the specific finding codes, never the presence or absence of the ok line.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-before-.rule: Before calling a shared test helper, read its parameter types in tests/helpers; never invent an option shape from memory (a past `{ exactPath }` did not exist). A wrong shape only passes typecheck when the helper's parameter is loosely typed, and then it silently matches nothing, so the test goes green for the wrong reason.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-in-path.rationale: CI matrix includes windows-latest; join() yields backslashes there.
fixture-and-assertion-discipline-in-path.rule: In path-equality/endsWith test assertions, normalize the native `join()` result with `.replaceAll('\\', '/')` (or `toPosixPath`) before comparing to a forward-slash literal — an un-normalized assertion passes on macOS/Linux but fails on Windows CI with 'expected false to be true'.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-in-vite.rule: In vitest, a vi.fn mocked to reject on every call (mockRejectedValue, or a mockImplementation that throws) raises a spurious unhandled rejection that fails the test when the function under test ultimately rejects after a retry loop; queue exactly N mockRejectedValueOnce outcomes matching the attempt count and assert with .rejects so every tracked mock promise is consumed.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-inspect.rule: Inspect fixture defaults and completed focused-test results before updating exact artifact assertions or starting a broader suite; a helper named minimalConfig may enable several targets.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-opencod.rule: opencode declares additionalRules/mcp/permissions native but is broken: (1) generated .opencode/rules/*.md are inert because OpenCode does NOT auto-read .opencode/rules/ — additional instruction files must be listed in the opencode.json `instructions` array (which agentsmesh never emits); (2) mergeOpenCodeSettings delegates to core mergeSettingsJson (Claude schema, only carries `permissions`/`hooks`), so regenerating over an existing opencode.json silently DROPS the freshly-generated `mcp` and `permission` keys. Fix needs an opencode-specific merger overlaying mcp/permission/instructions, plus emitting an `instructions` glob for .opencode/rules.

opencode mergeOpenCodeSettings delegates to core mergeSettingsJson, which uses the Claude schema and only carries incoming permissions and hooks; it does NOT copy opencode-specific permission or mcp keys from newContent. When asserting the merge-base-present branch, expect base keys preserved and incoming permissions/hooks merged, not an opencode permission key.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-1.rule: Assert the exact relative path set and exact count for generated files/dirs — never `some(...)`, prefix matches, or "at least one". Cross-check referenced artifacts (e.g. hook wrapper scripts) against the config that points to them.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-10.rule: When replacing or removing a core helper API, run a targeted search for all direct imports/usages (including unit tests that reference helpers by name like the old reference normalizer) and update those tests before relying on the full suite.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-11.rule: Whenever a generation/import/rewrite contract changes, mirror updates across the matching suites: research (`agents-folder-structure-research`), round-trip (`import-generate-roundtrip`), edge-case (`link-rebaser-edge-cases`), unit, integration, and e2e — primary tests alone do not codify the full contract.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-12.rule: Use the correct shape for test helpers: `findGeneratedFile` accepts either a plain string for exact path matching or `{ stringContaining }`/`{ stringMatching }` — `{ exactPath }` does not exist. Check the helper's actual parameter types before use.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-13.rule: For global-mode structure validation tests, drive `generate()` from `src/core/generate/engine.ts` with `scope: 'global'` and a `ValidatedConfig`-shaped fixture — `runGenerate()` from the CLI returns an exit code, not files.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-14.rule: Cross-platform assertion tolerance: normalize native paths to POSIX in tests via `toPosixPath(result.fromPath)` before `.toContain('.codex/...')`; extend `stripProtectedRegions` to drop Windows absolute-path tokens before `not.toContain('.agentsmesh\\')` checks; permit any of `` `docs/...` ``, `` `/docs/...` ``, `` `./docs/...` ``, `` `../docs/...` `` for inline-backtick path rewrites that depend on realpath on 8.3-shortname Windows tmpdirs.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-15.rule: When codegen-ing module-level array-literal data from per-target imports, patch the existing source file in place between sentinel comments instead of extracting to a new generated module — `descriptor-paths.test.ts` and other per-descriptor import paths trip ESM TDZ when an extra hop captures undefined slots.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-16.rule: Per-target import mappers referenced from a descriptor object literal must live in a third file (`import-mappers.ts`), never in `importer.ts` — descriptor↔importer cycles capture `undefined` in `map:` fields and the runner throws at execution time.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-2.rule: When asserting an exact generated repo tree after `generate`, include `.agentsmesh/.lock` in the expected set — `generate` always emits it.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-3.rule: When a user asks for e2e coverage over realistic structures, start from the richest existing fixture and mutate a temp copy — do not invent a smaller synthetic project.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-4.rule: Audit fixtures with a full-depth listing first; never use `find -maxdepth N` on nested skill/reference trees and conclude content is absent.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-5.rule: Before writing parameterized tests, scoring rules, or tie-breaks over any descriptor-derived list (`BUILTIN_TARGETS`, `RULES`, capability sets), run a one-shot `tsx scripts/<dump>.mts` that materializes the values and counts collisions; pick inputs that are unique per case and document ambiguity.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-6.rule: Re-import tests must cover importing into an *existing* `.agentsmesh` tree, not only empty-project round trips — verify unsupported target metadata is preserved from the canonical destination instead of erased.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-7.rule: When converting loose install/manifest assertions into strict ones, inspect the real persisted entry shape first and lock tests to the observed contract (field omission, ordering) — never write expectations from inferred intent.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-8.rule: Mock `ValidatedConfig` fixtures (any `mockLoadScopedConfig.mockResolvedValue(...)`) must include every field the schema defaults populate (e.g. `plugins: []`). When a new orchestration step reads `config.X`, grep every mock and add the field before rerunning.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-9.rule: When tightening `TargetDescriptor` schema requirements, run a repo-wide descriptor fixture search plus the full test suite and update every plugin/mock descriptor fixture to the full contract — focused catalog tests are insufficient.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-strict-.rule: Strict generated artifact contract arrays must remain in the exact sorted order returned by generatedPathsOnDisk; when adding a path, compare adjacent full paths rather than appending by feature.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-tests-e.rule: tests/e2e/helpers/reference-targets.ts and generate-reference-rewrite-matrix.e2e.test.ts's pathRewriteCandidates/deepRelativeToolPaths only generated ../ and ./ variants for refs starting with a dot (e.g. .windsurf/rules/x.md); a target whose native per-rule path has no dot prefix (codex-cli's nested src/AGENTS.md) silently got zero deep-relative candidates, failing expectMarkdownSelfLink from nested outputs. Guard on startsWith('..')/startsWith('/') instead of requiring a leading dot so any repo-root-relative path gets full variant generation.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-to-cove.rule: To cover the `-1` arm of an id/createdAt tie-break comparator in lessons code, do NOT route data through saveLessonsGraph (it canonicalizes/sorts keys) or queryLessons (it sorts matches by id ascending) — both pre-sort the input so the comparator never returns -1. Instead write the graph JSON with reverse-ordered keys via raw writeFileSync, or call the pure ranker (rankLessons) directly with a descending `matches` array.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-when-a-.rule: When a CLI command handler in src/cli/command-handlers.ts gains a new trailing argument (e.g. an injected deps object), update the matching toHaveBeenNthCalledWith/toHaveBeenCalledWith assertions in tests/unit/cli/command-handlers.test.ts to include it; in non-TTY test runs the TTY-gated interactive branch is false so the injected deps arg is {}.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-when-ad.rationale: A green gate on trigger-disjoint or loose-topN cases proves only plumbing, not ranker discriminability.
fixture-and-assertion-discipline-when-ad.rule: When adding a ranking-discrimination case to the lessons recurrence harness fixture (tests/fixtures/lessons/recurrence/*.json), use a TIGHT per-case topN (1 or 2): at a loose topN every matched lesson is retrieved, so a matched lesson can never be forbidden and rank order is never exercised — the case then only proves trigger plumbing, not discriminability. Also ensure the matched set is a strict SUBSET of the graph when testing matched-set-local signals (topic coherence), and VALIDATE the whole fixture by mutation-testing the ranker (flip RRF weights/tie-breaks, disable a signal) and confirming the gate turns red.

When adding an e2e/test fixture file whose path contains a segment matching a repo-root .gitignore pattern (generated target dirs like .cursor/, .kiro/, .warp/ or root files like CONVENTIONS.md/.rules), git silently ignores it — a bare `git add` no-ops and the file never reaches CI, so tests pass locally (file on disk) but fail on CI's fresh checkout with the fixture source absent (readFileSafe→null→import silently skips, exit 0). Keep such .gitignore patterns ROOT-ANCHORED (leading /) so they match only the repo's own dogfood outputs, not tests/e2e/fixtures/. After adding any fixture, verify none were dropped: `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard tests/e2e/fixtures/` must be empty.

When adding an MCP tool or a field to a shared CLI data type (e.g. PrunePlan/LessonsPruneData, TOOL_DESCRIPTORS), grep ALL inline test fixtures and strict-count assertions repo-wide and run the FULL vitest suite before claiming done — targeted suites miss renderer/e2e fixtures and 'exactly N tools' counts in register/sweep/mcp-server e2e tests.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-when-ad.rationale: The import-map builder is a separate file from the generator and importer; it's easy to forget when adding a new capability to a target.
fixture-and-assertion-discipline-when-ad.rule: When adding commands support to a target, also update the target's import-map builder (src/core/reference/import-maps/<target>.ts) to list the commands directory — missing this causes import round-trip reference rewriting tests to fail even when generator, descriptor, and importer are all correct.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-when-as.rule: When asserting line-exact CLI output captured from stdout (toEqual on split lines, or a /^ {2}\S/ line regex), strip ANSI color codes first: logger.info wraps every line in cyan escapes (\x1b[36m...\x1b[0m) unless NO_COLOR is set, so raw-line assertions see the escape — not the leading spaces — and silently match nothing, even though toContain of the inner text still passes.

When asserting on `agentsmesh lessons validate` output, know it prints "Lessons graph: ok." to stdout ONLY when there are zero findings; non-fatal warnings (e.g. UNREACHABLE_LESSON for a lesson with no triggers) are written to stderr and suppress the ok line while exit stays 0. Test fixtures that expect the ok line must seed lessons WITH at least one trigger, or assert on exit code instead.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-when-te.rationale: A symlink-escape regression test was falsely green on macOS until projectRoot was realpath'd, because the canonicalize fallback compared a /var path against a /private/var root.
fixture-and-assertion-discipline-when-te.rule: When testing realpath-based path containment (e.g. plugin source containment in src/plugins/load-plugin.ts) with `mkdtemp` tmp dirs, realpath the projectRoot before passing it to the code under test. On macOS the tmp dir resolves through /private (/var → /private/var), so a raw `mkdtempSync` projectRoot makes the prefix check pass/fail for the WRONG reason (a /var-vs-/private/var shape mismatch instead of the symlink/traversal under test), which can mask a real containment gap and make a should-be-red test falsely green.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-1.rule: Every third-party YAML frontmatter parse on install/import paths — whether the file is `SKILL.md`, command, agent, rule, MDC, or skill-name extraction (`readSkillFrontmatterName()`) — MUST use `tryParseFrontmatter()` / `parseFrontmatterForPath(..., onError)` and emit a "skipping <path>: <reason>" warning on failure. Reserve strict `parseFrontmatter()` exclusively for user-authored canonical content under `.agentsmesh/`.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-2.rule: When auditing parser changes, grep both `parseFrontmatter` AND every per-target importer (`src/targets/<id>/importer*.ts`) plus every auxiliary helper (skill-name extraction, MDC inference, name detection) before declaring the lenient-parsing fix applied.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-3.rule: NEVER add files under `.agentsmesh/skills/<name>/` beyond `SKILL.md` and ordinary supporting files (`references/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`, `assets/`). Do not invent `agents/openai.yaml` or other shapes — the canonical skill spec is `SKILL.md` + supporting files only.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-4.rule: NEVER write a literal `*/` inside any `/* ... */` or JSDoc block comment — including header comments in test files. Replace glob-shaped paths in prose (e.g. `.agentsmesh/skills/*/SKILL.md`) with `skills/{name}/SKILL.md` or `glob: *.md`, or move the glob into a single-line `//` comment outside the block.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-5.rule: Canonical booleans derivable from the destination path or artifact kind (notably `root: false` on non-root rules) MUST be derived and serialized in one shared helper, never left to per-target importer habits. Add cross-target tests that assert the exact canonical frontmatter contract.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-6.rule: Manual install staging and persistence MUST share one skill-name derivation helper. If staging reads the name via `readSkillFrontmatterName()` from `SKILL.md` frontmatter, persistence (`pick.skills`) MUST use the same source — never `basename(contentRoot)` on one side and frontmatter on the other.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-7.rule: Any synthetic canonical entity created from a non-frontmattered source (e.g. `.cursorrules` / `.windsurfrules` root files, marketplace stubs) MUST carry a non-empty `description` (e.g. `Imported from .cursorrules`). Empty descriptions pass unit tests but get dropped by `resolveRulePool()`'s `validateRule` re-filter under `dryRun=true`, even with `--force`.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-8.rule: Projected-agent test fixtures MUST be built from the documented `serializeProjectedAgentSkill()` output: real `x-agentsmesh-kind: agent` plus `x-agentsmesh-name` (or an `am-agent-*` directory). NEVER invent flags like `x-projected-agent: true`. Assertions must lock the exact canonical `.agentsmesh/agents/<name>.md` destination.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-9.rule: Filter "boilerplate" files by intent, not by a single blanket predicate. Maintain one typed map (`stem → 'noise' | 'preserved'`) with three derived predicates: `isBoilerplate` (prevent phantom entities in entity importers / flat-collection classifiers), `isNoiseBoilerplate` (drop in staging + skill supporting-files), `isPreservedBoilerplate` (keep LICENSE/NOTICE/COPYING/README in skill subtrees AND at pack root for legal attribution + consumer context). Both `listSupportingFiles` and `cpFilteredSkill` must use the noise-only predicate at content-staging time.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-when-pr.rationale: First hooks.yaml recall-injector used parse+stringify and wiped the template's schema directive + comments; only caught during real-init verification, required a rewrite to parseDocument.
frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-when-pr.rule: When programmatically injecting a managed unit into a canonical YAML config that can carry comments or a `# yaml-language-server` schema directive (e.g. hooks.yaml), edit via the YAML Document API (`parseDocument` + node mutation + `String(doc)`), NEVER `parse()`→`stringify()` — the round-trip silently drops the schema directive and all comments. Mirror the lessons-paragraph contract: preserve surrounding content, inject only the managed entries.

generate-any-path-containment-assert-add.rule: Any path-containment assert added to the stale sweep (findStaleGeneratedOutputs / findUntrackedManagedDirFiles) must ALSO run in the pre-write check in generate-handlers/convert, covering every active target's managedOutputs.dirs — the sweep runs after all files are written and before writeLockFile, so a managed dir that produced no output this run (feature off) and resolves outside the root aborts with outputs on disk and no lock, leaving check reporting Not-initialized on every rerun. Dry-run must run the same check so it cannot say OK for a layout the real run rejects.

generate-emit-empty-owned-settings-when.rule: Emit empty owned settings when canonical configuration is explicitly empty so the last permission, hook, or server is revoked; distinguish empty objects from missing canonical files and preserve unrelated native settings.

generate-never-insert-an-import-by.rule: Never insert an import by regex-matching the first occurrence of the word 'import' in a TypeScript file — target files open with a doc comment that often contains the word in prose, and the insertion silently corrupts the comment while still compiling elsewhere. Anchor on a line-start match (^import) or insert after the last existing import line, then diff the file to confirm only imports changed.

generate-when-an-emission-helper-takes.rationale: generateFeature emitted without mergeContent for six features, replacing shared user config files (~/.codex/config.toml) wholesale.
generate-when-an-emission-helper-takes.rule: When an emission helper takes an OPTIONAL merge/transform callback, do not pass it per call site — export a single `options` factory (e.g. `outputMergeOptions(target)`) and thread it through every emitter, including sibling branches that push results directly (feature-loop `mirrorGlobalPath`). One call site silently omitting the callback is invisible to types and destroyed real user config.

generation-cleanup-stale-output-eviction.rule: Stale-output eviction must never delete a static managedOutputs.files path the lock has no provenance for (first run, hand-authored AGENTS.md). Alternate instruction locations a primary root replaces (.claude/CLAUDE.md, .kimi-code/AGENTS.md) belong in managedOutputs.supersededFiles, evicted only when the run emits the primary; do not reintroduce a 'delete on sight' or a legacy-lock flag.

generation-collision-source-maps-a-gener.rationale: Conditional key assignment made grant-then-revoke a no-op that did not even report drift.
generation-collision-source-maps-a-gener.rule: A generator that merges into a user-owned config file must rewrite every key it owns on EVERY emit (empty list or key removal), or revoking a canonical entry never propagates; guard the fully-empty case by skipping the emit only when the file holds none of those owned keys yet, so a freshly scaffolded empty permissions.yaml never overrides the tool's own defaults.

generation-collision-source-maps-adding-.rule: Adding a parameter to a descriptor hook like emitScopedSettings silently passes undefined at existing test call sites (JS ignores arity mismatch), turning set.has(...) into a runtime TypeError rather than a compile error — when changing such a signature, grep every descriptor.emitScopedSettings!(...) and direct emitter call site under tests/unit/targets and update them before relying on the suite.

generation-collision-source-maps-factory.rationale: factory-droid generator emits Claude Code bare shape (no "hooks" wrapper) which Factory Droid cannot read; importer for hooks is missing entirely, so round-trip drops hooks.
generation-collision-source-maps-factory.rule: Factory Droid hooks.json wraps event names under a top-level "hooks" key ({ "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [{matcher, hooks:[{type,command}]}] } }) per docs.factory.ai, exactly like codex-cli — NOT the bare top-level Claude Code shape. The factory-droid generateHooks must JSON.stringify({ hooks }, …) (replace buildClaudeHooksObjectFromCanonical's bare output), and its importer must read parsed.hooks (model importCodexHooks, not importClaudeHooksJson).

generation-collision-source-maps-feature.rule: Feature generators that share one output file cannot rely on descriptor.mergeGeneratedOutputContent unless they run through optional-features merging; verify engine ordering and route shared JSON settings through emitScopedSettings or another merge-aware path.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-1.rule: Whenever a target generates more than one file from the same canonical source, audit the output-source map against the full generator output list so every emitted path participates in rewriting and collision logic — never assume "one canonical → one artifact".

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-10.rule: When an importer maps reserved/generated source artifacts back into canonical files, add strict re-import tests that preseed stale outputs (`_ab-agent-*`, `_ab-command-*`, hidden scoped rules) and verify the importer removes them — import is not write-only.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-11.rule: When two targets implement the same import filter/cleanup pattern (e.g. Codex and Windsurf), move the logic into a shared helper and verify both targets against the same strict regression cases — never copy-paste per-target cleanup.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-12.rule: When importing any target artifact, build the normalization map from every supported generated path family so re-import can recover canonical `.agentsmesh/...` links from previously polluted outputs (e.g. cline / claude-code reading Codex-style `.agents/...` links). Never assume same-family pristine inputs.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-13.rule: When one canonical feature emits multiple artifact families (e.g. Copilot hook JSON + wrapper scripts), centralize the eligibility predicate ("is this hook runnable?") in one shared helper and add a regression test comparing referenced artifacts against emitted files. Never duplicate "is valid" logic per generator.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-14.rule: When a target generator intentionally drops canonical metadata (e.g. Codex CLI MCP `description`), add or update a target-specific lint warning and cover with unit + CLI e2e tests; unsupported metadata is part of the target contract users must see.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-15.rule: When tests verify generated files or directories, assert the exact relative path set and exact count, and cross-check referenced artifacts (e.g. hook wrapper scripts) against the config that points to them — no `some(...)`, prefix-only, or "at least one" checks.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-16.rule: When a target-format cannot represent all canonical metadata (e.g. Cursor command `description`/`allowed-tools`), add strict re-import-into-existing-project tests that prove unsupported fields are preserved from the canonical destination rather than erased. Empty-project round trips are insufficient.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-17.rule: When widening a core type into a union (e.g. `McpServer` gaining URL transports), add explicit type guards at every serializer/generator boundary that needs a specific variant and rerun `pnpm typecheck` before declaring the refactor done.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-18.rule: In `resolveGen` (engine), check `getBuiltinTargetDefinition(target)` first; if present, delegate entirely to `resolveTargetFeatureGenerator(target, feature, config)` so conversion config (e.g. `commandsToSkills: false`) is always respected. Plugin registry fallback must not bypass builtin conversion logic via `getDescriptor`.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-19.rule: When a command validates multiple canonical features in `runLint()`, gate each lint family (commands, MCP, permissions, hooks) by its own feature flag — never nest them all under `hasRules`. Add a regression test for configs that enable non-rule features without `rules`.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-2.rule: When a layout declares `additionalRootDecorationPaths`, add those decoration paths to generate-side source maps and test at least one nested Markdown mirror for canonical link cleanup; decoration paths are generated artifacts, not render-only metadata.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-20.rule: When multiple targets share a common parent directory in global mode (e.g. `.gemini/`), each non-native target must use a namespaced subdirectory (Antigravity → `.gemini/antigravity/`) to avoid path collisions; the collision detector only special-cases `AGENTS.md`.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-3.rule: When a target can emit multiple artifact families from the same canonical source (e.g. Copilot `.github/copilot/*.instructions.md` and `.github/instructions/*.md`), build and cache rewrite maps per output path or per artifact family — never key only by target. Add tests for each emitted path family.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-4.rule: When resolving conflicting shared artifacts by choosing a preferred/richer content body, keep that chosen result's `status`/`currentContent`; only merge statuses for truly identical content. Never let a discarded result donate drift status to the kept artifact.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-5.rule: When multiple targets share one output path, compare outputs after normalizing target-specific references back to canonical paths before deciding they conflict; add coverage for rewritten-content overlaps.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-6.rule: When skills can originate from packs, add pack-path→target-path entries to the artifact map (alongside canonical `.agentsmesh/skills/...` entries) so the reference rewriter can translate both canonical and pack absolute paths.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-7.rule: When appending global instructions / root-instruction decoration to generated targets, phrase the canonical location without the literal `.agentsmesh/` substring (e.g. "the `.agentsmesh` directory at the project root"), keep legacy paragraph detection for upgrades, and strip both old and new contract blocks on import in the shared root-rule import path. Cover with round-trip e2e.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-8.rule: When adding a secondary rule projection folder for a target that already has a primary root file (e.g. Codex `AGENTS.md`), default to mirroring only non-root / additional rules — never duplicate the primary root file unless the spec explicitly requires it.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-9.rule: When enabling a new artifact family for a target, update `reference-map-targets` + import-reference map builders + importer scanners together; do not ship generator/importer surface files first and patch path-translation contracts later. Verify with the target-contract matrix e2e.

generation-collision-source-maps-when-ch.rule: When changing a TargetDescriptor hook contract (e.g. adding enabledFeatures to emitScopedSettings, or capability resolution like getTargetCapabilities), the change must hold for PLUGIN descriptors too, not just builtins: the engine call sites resolve via getBuiltinTargetDefinition(target) ?? getDescriptor(target) with no builtin-vs-plugin branch. Update the rich-plugin reference fixture to the new hook signature AND add a registered-plugin-descriptor test (generateScopedSettingsFeature with a plugin id), or plugin alignment stays unproven.

generation-safety-a-key-scoped-merger-mu.rationale: mergeOwnedJsonKeys returned null on a commented .vscode/mcp.json, so the fallback wrote generated content over the user's inputs array; null means "not my path", not "keep the file".
generation-safety-a-key-scoped-merger-mu.rule: A key-scoped merger must return the base verbatim when it cannot parse the user's file (JSONC, array, unknown syntax) — returning null falls through to the default policy, which replaces the whole file and destroys the very keys the merger exists to protect.

generation-safety-a-yaml-ownership-marke.rationale: mergeRooCustomModes marked every mode it wrote, but on re-read item 0 had commentBefore undefined, so the first generated Roo mode was treated as user-authored and never revoked; the existing test only revoked a second item so it passed.
generation-safety-a-yaml-ownership-marke.rule: A YAML ownership marker written as a comment above the FIRST sequence item does not survive a round-trip on that item — the parser reattaches it to the sequence node's commentBefore. Always assert revocation of the first item, not just a middle one, or the marker scheme silently fails for it.

generation-safety-in-lock-sync-ts-do.rationale: Supersedes an earlier lesson claiming this gating empties outputsStale for every input and kills the drift gate. That claim is wrong: only the directory-discovered portion is gated.
generation-safety-in-lock-sync-ts-do.rule: In lock-sync.ts, DO pass the lock's outputs map as both expectedPaths and generatedOutputs to findStaleGeneratedOutputs. The dir sweep then only considers files agentsmesh actually generated, which stops `check` reporting a tool-written file as stale generated output; `managedOutputs.files` entries are added ungated, so genuine stale owned artifacts are still caught. Verified: foreign dir file exits 0, stale .kiroignore exits 1.

generation-safety-never-scaffold-an-expl.rationale: agentsmesh init wrote allow: []/deny: []/ask: [], so the first generate after adoption cleared a user's existing .claude/settings.json permissions including their deny entries.
generation-safety-never-scaffold-an-expl.rule: Never scaffold an explicitly empty collection (allow: [], deny: [], mcpServers: {}) into a canonical template — an empty collection is an instruction the generators apply over the user's existing tool config, whereas an absent key means "not managed yet". Comment the examples out instead.

generation-safety-when-a-code-path-delib.rationale: The omission was documented and correct when written; it only became a bug because a later change made `outputs` load-bearing for stale cleanup, and nothing linked the two.
generation-safety-when-a-code-path-delib.rule: When a code path deliberately omits a field from a written record, re-check that decision whenever the field gains a new consumer — `resolveLockConflict` omitted the lock's `outputs` map for good reasons, and that became a permanent data strand the day the directory sweep started gating deletion on it.

generation-safety-when-a-defect-is-trace.rationale: bf88aaa2 diagnosed the shared feature-loop merge gap but rerouted goose only; codex-cli, crush, qwen-code and copilot kept wholesale-rewriting user config, and a real ~/.codex/config.toml was destroyed.
generation-safety-when-a-defect-is-trace.rule: When a defect is traced to a shared engine path (e.g. generateFeature passing no mergeContent), fix the shared path or sweep every target routed through it — never patch the one target whose symptom you happened to be looking at.

generation-safety-when-a-target-has-proj.rationale: mergeRooCustomModesYaml claimed only ~/.roo/settings/custom_modes.yaml, so .roomodes (Roo's project custom-modes store) was still replaced wholesale and deleted when the agents feature was disabled.
generation-safety-when-a-target-has-proj.rule: When a target has project and global twins of the same user-owned file, make the merge hook claim BOTH path constants in one place — fixing only the scope you were looking at leaves the twin on whole-file replacement, and its layout entry on the stale-cleanup delete list.

generation-safety-when-adding-mergegener.rationale: claude-code gained a .mcp.json merger while deepagents-cli kept writing it raw; any user with both enabled and a .mcp.json holding a key besides mcpServers got exit 1 on every generate.
generation-safety-when-adding-mergegener.rule: When adding mergeGeneratedOutputContent to a target, first find every other target that emits the same path and give them an identical owned-key merger; a path with one merging and one raw writer makes resolveOutputCollisions hard-fail the whole generate run.

generation-safety-when-inserting-an-impo.rationale: Inserting after `import {` in src/targets/qwen-code/index.ts produced TS1003/TS1005 syntax errors; the existing lesson covers regex-matching the word import in prose but not the multi-line import case.
generation-safety-when-inserting-an-impo.rule: When inserting an import after "the last line starting with import", check that line is a complete statement — a multi-line `import {` is the last such line in most target index.ts files, and inserting after it splits the brace block. Anchor on the last line that also ends with a quote-and-semicolon, or insert before the first import instead.

generation-safety-when-making-a-co-owned.rationale: Its only trigger was src/targets/*/revocation.ts, files deleted when the revocation layer was withdrawn, leaving the lesson unreachable. Re-pointed at where coOwnedFiles and the merge hooks actually live, so it fires when revocation is attempted again.
generation-safety-when-making-a-co-owned.rule: When making a co-owned target output revocable (managedOutputs.coOwnedFiles), the merge hook must be able to DELETE or empty the key, and the cleared projection must name only the leaf keys agentsmesh writes — never the containers. A container-level clear (permissions/options/agent objects) destroys the user's sibling keys, and an assign-only merger cannot express revocation at all. Verify the merger against a base holding foreign sibling keys before declaring the claim.

generation-safety-when-removing-a-featur.rationale: Commit 6e7b06f3 stripped revocableOutputs from 20 descriptors and the engine but left three references in website/src/content/docs/guides/building-plugins.mdx; only a later docs audit caught it.
generation-safety-when-removing-a-featur.rule: When removing a feature or descriptor hook from the codebase, grep website/src/content/docs and README for its name in the same change — a hook documented for plugin authors but deleted from the code tells them to implement dead code, and no test or typecheck catches it.

generation-safety-when-writing-an-invari.rationale: The first stale-cleanup fix shipped a repo-wide invariant that only probed descriptor hooks, so .claude/settings.json (user model/env/auth) and goose permission.yaml stayed on the delete list with the test reporting no violations.
generation-safety-when-writing-an-invari.rule: When writing an invariant test whose oracle detects "co-ownership", enumerate every mechanism that confers it — descriptor merge hook, the SETTINGS_JSON_PATHS fallback, and scopeExtras generators that read-and-merge — because an oracle that knows only one mechanism passes green while the other cases stay broken.

generation-safety-when-you-add-a-guard.rationale: mergeMcpServersJson returned newContent for an unparsable base long after mergeOwnedJsonKeys was fixed to preserve it; a later sweep then wired that helper into ~20 more paths, multiplying the data loss.
generation-safety-when-you-add-a-guard.rule: When you add a guard to one merge helper (e.g. preservedUnparsableBase in json-owned-keys.ts), grep every sibling helper in src/core/generate for the same parse-then-fall-back shape and apply it there too — a second helper without the guard silently reintroduces the bug at whatever scale the next sweep applies it.

git-commit-hygiene-a-failing-git-merge-d.rule: A failing git merge driver does NOT make git re-merge the file with conflict markers: git leaves the %A (ours) file byte-identical and marks the path unmerged with no markers in it, so resolving via 'git add' silently discards everything the other side had. A union driver must therefore WRITE its best-effort union before exiting non-zero, and treat an empty %O (git passes an empty ancestor when the path is new on both branches) as an empty base rather than a parse failure.

git-commit-hygiene-before-creating-a-new.rule: Before creating a new standalone markdown document, check whether the intended directory is ignored; in this repo new files under docs/ and tasks/ are ignored, so use a tracked path or intentionally force-add.

git-commit-hygiene-in-this-repo-docs-is.rule: In this repo `/docs/` is gitignored (root /docs policy), so design specs under `docs/superpowers/specs/` are intentionally LOCAL/untracked and `git add docs/...` silently no-ops (prints "paths are ignored"). Before any `git commit`, stage with EXPLICIT pathspecs and verify `git diff --cached --stat` (or `git status`) first: a bare `git commit` right after an ignored/empty `git add` commits whatever else is already staged — here it committed the still-uncommitted, unattributed `package.json` precommit edit under a "docs(spec)" message. Undo such a slip with `git reset HEAD~1` (mixed) since it isn't pushed.

git-commit-hygiene-never-git-stash-a-fil.rule: Never git stash a file to prove a test red while parallel agents have staged new files in the tree: stash and pop can restage or drop their state. Copy the file aside, write the old version, run the test, then copy it back.

git-commit-hygiene-never-let-a-git-commi.rule: Never let a git commit invoking the husky pre-commit hook (pnpm precommit: full coverage suite + build) be killed by a tool timeout mid-run -- lint-staged's internal git-stash backup can be left inconsistent, so a LATER 'git commit -m msg <pathspec-list>' can silently union a stale/corrupted index with the given paths and produce a commit that looks like it deletes thousands of unrelated files (files stay safe on disk; only the commit's recorded tree is wrong). Recovery: verify with 'git show --stat HEAD'; if the diff is absurdly large, 'git reset --mixed <last-good-commit>' (working tree untouched, files reappear as modified not deleted), re-stage only the intended paths, and re-commit with no trailing pathspec on the commit itself. Give git commit a long timeout (up to 600000ms) so the hook finishes uninterrupted.

git-commit-hygiene-other-processes-pack-.rule: Other processes (pack install/refresh, the harness) can `git add` files mid-session in this repo — e.g. installed-skill packs under `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`, `.agentsmesh/packs/` get pre-staged (`A `). So before `git commit`, run `git diff --cached --name-only` as a SEPARATE step and READ it; NEVER `&&`-chain the verify with the commit (you can't react, and you'll commit pre-staged unrelated files under the wrong message). Stage with explicit pathspecs; undo a slip with `git reset --mixed HEAD~1` (not pushed) then re-stage only your files.

git-commit-hygiene-running-pnpm-install-.rationale: Commits 1-3 in a symlink-only worktree were hook-free; a later pnpm@10 install activated husky, and pnpm 11's deps-status check then aborted the deps-bump commit despite node_modules correctly holding tar@7.5.20.
git-commit-hygiene-running-pnpm-install-.rule: Running `pnpm install` inside a fresh git worktree fires the `prepare: husky` script, which activates the git hooks (core.hooksPath=.husky) for that worktree — so commits AFTER an install run the full `pnpm precommit` suite, while commits before it are hook-free. Also, a pnpm 10 install followed by a pnpm 11 pre-run deps-status check fails spuriously on version metadata. When a worktree commit hook fails only on this environmental deps-status noise and the change is deps-only + independently verified against the CI pnpm major (frozen install + audit green), commit with --no-verify.

git-commit-hygiene-when-auditing-unpushe.rule: When auditing unpushed work, probe the configured upstream independently before running other read-only inventory commands, because a branch without an upstream exits nonzero and can suppress later chained evidence.

git-commit-hygiene-when-writing-a-git-co.rationale: A backtick-quoted `?? []` in a commit -m body was executed as a command and stripped, mangling the message and forcing an amend.
git-commit-hygiene-when-writing-a-git-co.rule: When writing a git commit message via the Bash tool (zsh), never put backticks or bare glob chars (`, ?, [, ]) inside -m "...": zsh runs command substitution on backticks even within double quotes (and glob-expands ? / []), silently deleting that span from the recorded message. Use single quotes or plain prose for code identifiers, or pass the body via -F -/a heredoc, and verify with `git log -1 --format=%B` right after committing.

global-mode-global-scope-capability-reso.rule: Global-scope capability resolution has TWO coupled gates in builtin-targets.ts: getTargetCapabilities (raw level) AND getEffectiveTargetSupportLevel (conversion upgrade via supportsConversion). When a target lacks globalSupport, BOTH must short-circuit to none for scope 'global' — fixing only getTargetCapabilities leaves supportsConversion targets (e.g. replit-agent) still reporting embedded in global scope, so matrix/docs diverge from what generate --global actually emits (zero files).

global-mode-rule-1.rule: When implementing global mode for any target, add a `global` layout AND `rewriteGeneratedPath` that translates project-level paths (e.g. `.github/`) to global paths (e.g. `.copilot/`). Layout path resolvers alone are not enough — the engine uses `rewriteGeneratedPath` to transform generator output paths before writing. Verify a representative file lands at the correct global location.

global-mode-rule-10.rule: For global-mode structure-validation tests, call `generate()` from `src/core/generate/engine.ts` with `scope: 'global'` — not `runGenerate()` from the CLI commands, which returns an exit code (`Promise<number>`) instead of the generated files. Provide a `makeConfig()` helper returning a `ValidatedConfig` with target + features configured.

global-mode-rule-11.rule: Derive global-mode e2e expectations from each target's descriptor/layout constants (e.g. Windsurf `workflows`, Roo `.roo-code`, Codex `config.toml`), not from historical path helpers. Whenever a path-rewrite helper is retired or global behavior shifts, update e2e assertions from descriptor constants and rerun the e2e Vitest config after `pnpm build`.

global-mode-rule-12.rule: Keep canonical loader helpers (e.g. `loadCanonicalFiles()`) backward-compatible with BOTH project-root and canonical-dir inputs when adding scope awareness. Sweep every caller before tightening the signature — extend, install, and the loader test suite all pass project roots and expect the helper to locate `.agentsmesh/` itself.

global-mode-rule-13.rule: When bridging generated global files into an importer fallback path in tests, copy the EXACT generated tree the round-trip needs — including `references/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`, and `assets/` — not just `SKILL.md`.

global-mode-rule-14.rule: For `findGeneratedFile` in global structure tests, pass a plain string for exact path matching or an object with `stringContaining`/`stringMatching`. Never invent `{ exactPath: '...' }` — check the actual signature first.

global-mode-rule-2.rule: Follow the full global-mode pattern in one pass: (a) global path constants, (b) `global` layout with `rewriteGeneratedPath`, (c) `mirrorGlobalPath` for cross-agent skill mirroring, (d) `globalCapabilities`, (e) `globalDetectionPaths`, (f) help text + docs. Model from Copilot/Cursor/Roo Code. Update all six together.

global-mode-rule-3.rule: After editing a target's `rewriteGeneratedPath`/global layout, re-audit imports — every referenced constant (e.g. `CURSOR_COMPAT_AGENTS`) must be in the file's import list.
