Run `pnpm typecheck` and the target's `generate --global` CLI test; treat missing-symbol imports as a release gate.

global-mode-rule-4.rule: When implementing global mode, import every required type (`TargetCapabilities`, `TargetLayout`) from `target.interface.js` and run `pnpm typecheck` immediately after adding the global layout. Do not assume copy-pasted patterns carried all imports.

global-mode-rule-5.rule: Namespace global paths under shared parent directories so multiple targets do not collide. If multiple targets share `.gemini/`, `.agents/`, etc., each non-native one MUST use a namespaced subdirectory (e.g. Antigravity → `.gemini/antigravity/`, Gemini CLI native → `.gemini/`). The collision detector only special-cases `AGENTS.md`; other shared-path collisions throw.

global-mode-rule-6.rule: In `import` flows, when `scope === 'global'`, only read tool-native subtrees under the home root (e.g. `~/.codex`, `~/.agents/skills`). Never run whole-tree `readDirRecursive` / `importFileDirectory` from `homedir()` — that blows the stack on symlink cycles (e.g. `~/.cache`) and scans the entire home tree. Add a `scope === 'global'` guard.

global-mode-rule-7.rule: In any helper that fakes the home directory via env (`HOME`) for `--global` e2e, on `process.platform === 'win32'` ALSO set `USERPROFILE` (and defensively `HOMEDRIVE`/`HOMEPATH`) from the same path, because `os.homedir()` on Windows reads `USERPROFILE`, not `HOME`. Put this in the spawn helper, not at call sites.

global-mode-rule-8.rule: For temp-dir symlink helpers that stage a fake home (e.g. `createTempProjectRoot(homedir())`), only symlink dot-entries (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, …) and root-level files. Never symlink non-dot directories like `Desktop`/`Documents` — listings/walks over the project root (`listScopedAgentsFiles`, the 18-target normalizer) will traverse them and hang.

global-mode-rule-9.rule: For `mirrorGlobalPath` skip/dual-mirror tests, derive eligibility from the run's actively-generated targets, not the configured set. `feature-loop.ts` passes the post-filter `targets` array to `mirrorGlobalPath`; using `targetFilter: ['copilot']` removes codex-cli from "active" even when it is in `config.targets`. To exercise the codex-cli skip, list both targets in `config.targets` and DO NOT pass `targetFilter`.

imports-before-importing-a-named-symbol.rule: Before importing a named symbol from a barrel/re-export module (e.g. target-ids.ts), grep that the symbol is actually re-exported there; target-ids.ts re-exports TARGET_IDS/BuiltinTargetId/isBuiltinTargetId but BUILTIN_TARGET_IDS lived only in builtin-target-ids-generated.ts — add the explicit re-export or import from the generated source.

init-clack-prompts-has-no-native.rationale: Clack's high-level confirm/multiselect can't express a back gesture, so back must be modeled by the caller.
init-clack-prompts-has-no-native.rule: @clack/prompts has no native "back" navigation. Implement wizard step-back as a state machine: a steps array + index loop (forward on 'next', index-1 on 'back'), persist answers so a revisited step restores them, and render yes/no questions as a select with a "↩ Back" option (not confirm). Put any multiselect step FIRST — a multiselect can't cleanly carry a Back choice.

init-enforce-project-only-invariants-e.rationale: The --lessons/--global throw in runInit didn't cover applyInitPlan, which scaffolded lessons whenever plan.lessons was true regardless of scope.
init-enforce-project-only-invariants-e.rule: Enforce project-only invariants (e.g. lessons) at the shared writer/primitive (applyInitPlan), not only at the CLI flag guard — a shared writer reachable by other callers (a future global wizard) bypasses the flag check, so guard `plan.scope === 'project'` where the side effect actually happens.

init-the-lessons-scaffold-result-shape.rationale: Adding gitattributesUpdated required editing the interface in init.ts and the inline structural dup in command-result.ts; only the renderer usage surfaced the miss via tsc.
init-the-lessons-scaffold-result-shape.rule: The lessons scaffold result shape is defined TWICE — ScaffoldLessonsResult in src/lessons/init.ts and a structural duplicate as InitData.lessons in src/cli/command-result.ts. When adding/removing a field, update BOTH: tsc only flags the renderer that READS a missing field, not the duplicated type definition, so a field added to one side silently type-checks until the renderer breaks.

init-the-standalone-agentsmesh-import-co.rationale: The growth plan drafted "npx agentsmesh import → found your configs" but import needs --from; the auto-detect import is an init feature. Caught by checking import --help before writing docs.
init-the-standalone-agentsmesh-import-co.rule: The standalone `agentsmesh import` command REQUIRES `--from <target>` and imports exactly one tool — it does NOT auto-detect. The auto-detect-and-import-all-existing-configs behavior lives in `agentsmesh init` (interactive wizard import step) and `agentsmesh init --yes` (non-interactive). When writing README/website/marketing copy, do not present bare `agentsmesh import` (or `npx agentsmesh import`) as an auto-detecting "import everything" command — lead the existing-repo path with `init`/`init --yes`.

init-when-making-a-cli-scope.rationale: Two integration tests asserting "global ignores the prompter / never enters the wizard" became contradictory once global became interactive.
init-when-making-a-cli-scope.rule: When making a CLI scope interactive that was previously non-interactive (e.g. enabling the global init wizard), grep for and rewrite the existing tests that asserted the OLD non-interactive behavior for that scope — they become silently wrong. Assert the new behavior (wizard entered, which prompts are asked vs skipped), don't just add new tests beside the stale ones.

install-import-pickers-agentsmesh-init-t.rule: agentsmesh init target selection is evidence-based, not breadth-based: --targets, --all-targets, project config, machine installs (descriptor global detection paths against $HOME), then the minimal set from descriptors declaring minimalInitDefault. Because init reads $HOME, any unit test exercising runInit MUST stub HOME/USERPROFILE to an empty dir or results vary per developer machine. buildConfig() now requires a non-empty target list; resolveInitTargets guarantees it.

install-import-pickers-allocate-pack-sta.rationale: Regression tests proved installing pack deletes separately installed pack.tmp and pack.old with local edits when sibling paths are reused for staging.
install-import-pickers-allocate-pack-sta.rule: Allocate pack staging and backups in an exclusively created operation directory; never delete fixed name-derived .tmp or .old siblings, because those are valid independent pack names. Clean only owned paths, and retain a backup when rollback fails.

install-import-pickers-canonical-paths-a.rule: Canonical paths are last-import-wins EXCEPT .agentsmesh/rules/_root.md and mcp.json, which accumulate. Root rule merging lives in the single shared serializer serializeImportedRuleWithFallback (src/targets/import/import-metadata-core.ts) because all ~45 root write sites across 33 targets funnel through it — never patch per-target importers for root-rule behavior. When changing it, remember the init placeholder body (src/canonical/root-rule-placeholder.ts) must count as unwritten or every import stacks under scaffold boilerplate.

install-import-pickers-every-per-target-.rule: Every per-target MCP importer/mapper must handle the full McpServer union — a command (stdio) branch AND a url (http/sse) branch; a stdio-only mapper that requires command silently drops remote URL/SSE servers on the generate->import round-trip, so audit and fix all sibling target mappers when fixing one. Prefer reusing the shared parseMcpJson over per-target reimplementations.

install-import-pickers-install-sync-refr.rule: install --sync / refresh re-run install from a SHA-pinned source, so the bridge must thread the PRIOR installs.yaml entry's original_ref AND persisted elevated consent (accepted_elevated) back through InstallReplayScope — otherwise a branch pin freezes to a SHA after the first refresh and sync silently strips previously-consented hooks/permissions/mcp while features still claims them. Also: recorded features must derive from the POST-strip canonical (featuresAfterStrip), not the pre-strip list, or partial consent desyncs features from pack contents even on first install.

install-import-pickers-lessons-hook-reca.rule: Lessons hook recall has two distinct caps and they are not interchangeable: HOOK_INJECT_LIMIT (5, src/lessons/hook-emit.ts) overrides the configured recallLimit, and recallMaxTokens (default 1200) is the token budget applied after the count slice. On a large graph the COUNT cap almost always binds, so any truncation message must attribute which cap fired before naming a knob. Separately, the hook path has no read-only classifier by default: use isReadOnlyCommand (src/lessons/read-only-command.ts) before recordFailure and before recurrenceEscalation, or read-only classes like cmd:cat and cmd:grep dominate the failure log and trigger false RECURRENT FAILURE banners.

install-import-pickers-rule-1.rule: Treat `as` on `InstallTarget` as a routing decision, not a feature label. Only set `as` for **flat-collection** sub-packs (no `skillPack`/`rootSkill` marker); leave `as` undefined for skill-pack / root-skill sub-packs so recursion re-runs auto-discovery at the sub-pack root. Always plumb `report.subPackFailures` into `InstallData` so the CLI renderer surfaces partial failures.

install-import-pickers-rule-10.rule: Manual install persistence and staging must share one skill-name derivation. If staging uses `readSkillFrontmatterName()`, persistence must use the same helper — never `basename(contentRoot)`.

install-import-pickers-rule-11.rule: When manual skill replay carries `pick.skills: [name]` but `path` is a collection root (e.g. `skills` or `skills/engineering`), search **all descendant `SKILL.md` paths** under the source root and stage the exact matched skill directories. Don't restrict to umbrella folders that themselves have `SKILL.md`.

install-import-pickers-rule-12.rule: Replay/scoped install narrowing must reach `installAsPack()` — pass the narrowed canonical through every downstream write/materialization path so unrelated settings (`mcp`, `permissions`, `hooks`, `ignore`) don't leak into the resulting pack.

install-import-pickers-rule-13.rule: Provide an explicit `--as` override that bypasses native-path heuristics; keep native auto-detection as fallback. Install discovery must not be coupled to target-native directory layouts for arbitrary folders.

install-import-pickers-rule-14.rule: Native install discovery is **read-only staging**. Import into a temporary staged copy and derive folder/file scope from importer `fromPath` results — never mutate the source checkout or heuristically traverse it for subtree selection.

install-import-pickers-rule-15.rule: Incremental pack updates must match by **stable remote identity** (provider + repo/url without ref), not the pinned `github:org/repo@sha`. Refresh stored `source`/`version` metadata after each successful merge. Preserve existing on-disk cache paths when refactoring cache-backed providers.

install-import-pickers-rule-16.rule: Single-file remote install parsing must cover both `tree/...` (directory) and `blob/...` (file) URLs per supported host.

install-import-pickers-rule-17.rule: Pack coverage must include settings features (`mcp`, `permissions`, `hooks`, `ignore`) — not just array resources. Write → load → generate tests must include a real non-dry-run command path.

install-import-pickers-rule-18.rule: Synthetic root-rule canonical entries (`.cursorrules`, `.windsurfrules`, marketplace stubs) MUST carry a non-empty `description` (e.g. `Imported from .cursorrules`) so they survive the dry-run-only re-validation pass in `pool-resolution.ts` (`resolveRulePool` filters by `validateRule` when `dryRun=true`).

install-import-pickers-rule-19.rule: Boilerplate filtering splits intent via one typed map (`stem → 'noise' | 'preserved'`) and three derived predicates: `isBoilerplate` (any — used by entity importers + flat-collection classifier to prevent README/LICENSE from becoming phantom entities), `isNoiseBoilerplate` (drop in staging + skill supporting-files), `isPreservedBoilerplate` (keep in skill subtrees). Both `listSupportingFiles` (canonical/features/skills.ts) AND `cpFilteredSkill` (install/source/skill-repo-filter.ts) must use the noise-only predicate at content-staging time.

install-import-pickers-rule-2.rule: Every third-party frontmatter parser on the install/import path — including auxiliary helpers like skill-name extraction (`readSkillFrontmatterName`) and `.mdc` inference (`inferMdcTarget`, `normalizeMdcToCanonical`) — must use `tryParseFrontmatter()` / `parseFrontmatterForPath(..., onError)` and degrade with a "skipping <path>: <reason>" warning. Reserve strict `parseFrontmatter()` for user-authored canonical content. Audit by grepping both `parseFrontmatter` and every `src/targets/<id>/importer*.ts`.

install-import-pickers-rule-20.rule: Plumb upstream `contentRoot` end-to-end (`runSinglePackInstall → executeRunInstallPoolsAndWrite → installAsPack → materializePack/mergeIntoPack`) so `collectPreservedRootFiles(contentRoot)` harvests top-level `README*` / `LICENSE*` / `NOTICE*` / `COPYING*` / `COPYRIGHT*` into the pack root **before** `hashPackContent` runs — preserved files must participate in `content_hash` + the per-file install manifest so uninstall removes them automatically.

install-import-pickers-rule-21.rule: `OUTPUT_DIR_TO_FEATURE` and `stripMarkdownExt` in `src/core/reference/validate-generated-markdown-links.ts` must enumerate every target-specific dir (`droids`, `instructions`, `prompts`, `steering`, …) and every double-extension (`.agent.md`, `.instructions.md`, `.prompt.md`) so `canonicalKeyFromOutputPath` produces the same canonical key as the source entity. Treat as a single-source-of-truth table: new target = one row each.

install-import-pickers-rule-22.rule: Wrap the terminal `runGenerate()` in **both** `runInstall` and `runUninstall` in try/catch (extracted as `runPostOperationGenerate('install' | 'uninstall', scope, rootBase)` in `src/install/run/post-install-generate.ts`). Downgrade failures to `logger.warn(...)` naming the failure mode — the pack + `installs.yaml` writes are the user's intent and must survive validator brittleness. Same rule for any future best-effort post-operation step (e.g. post-install `agentsmesh lint`).

install-import-pickers-rule-23.rule: Per-target skill-import dispatch loops belong behind one `importSkillsDirectory(options, recognizers[])` orchestrator with factory recognizers (`projectedAgentRecognizer`, `commandSkillRecognizer`) that own their own destination write + stale cleanup. Per-target adapters collapse to a config object + recognizer list so new targets can't drift on cleanup order or recognizer ordering.

install-import-pickers-rule-24.rule: When persisting strict install manifest assertions, inspect the **actual serialized entry shape** first (including field omission and ordering) — don't write expectations from inferred intent. Whenever the manifest type gains required fields, sweep all `toHaveBeenCalledWith` / deep-equality assertions, not just the typed fixture.

install-import-pickers-rule-25.rule: Whenever pack/install manifest persistence semantics change, rerun the full agents/commands/rules/skills matrix and the sibling-item amend cases — not only the user-reported entity.

install-import-pickers-rule-26.rule: Skill-pack integration fixtures with broken links must narrow the project's `features:` so the linking entity is NOT generated (e.g. `features: [rules]` when the broken link sits in a skill). Assert pack body + manifest there, not generated target files. Cross-protocol identity assertions (https/ssh/`github:` shorthand) belong in unit tests on `findExistingInstallName`, not integration.

install-import-pickers-rule-27.rule: Mock `ValidatedConfig` fixtures returned by `mockLoadScopedConfig.mockResolvedValue` must include every schema-defaulted field (`plugins: []`, etc.) because tests bypass schema validation. Adding any new orchestration step that reads `config.X` requires grepping for every mock and adding the field before rerunning.

install-import-pickers-rule-28.rule: Global import (`scope === 'global'`) must NOT pass `homedir()` as `projectRoot` for recursive scans. Only read tool-native subtrees under home (e.g. `~/.codex`, `~/.agents/skills`); never `readDirRecursive(homedir())` — symlink cycles under `~/.cache` will blow the stack.

install-import-pickers-rule-29.rule: Importers must clean stale reserved artifacts on re-import (e.g. `_ab-agent-*`, `_ab-command-*`, scoped-rule names). Extract shared filter/cleanup into one helper instead of copy-pasting per target. Import normalization must build the rewrite map from **every supported generated path family** so cross-target re-import recovers canonical `.agentsmesh/...` links from previously polluted outputs.

install-import-pickers-rule-3.rule: Normalize empty-string CLI flags (`path`, `target`, `as`) to `undefined` inside `readInstallFlags`. Picker auto-pick recursion in `run-install-locked.ts` builds nested flag bags with `target ?? ''`; the rest of the pipeline assumes "undefined OR non-empty".

install-import-pickers-rule-30.rule: When a target-native filename changes, update generation/docs to the new path but keep importer fallbacks for the previous on-disk filename unless the migration is explicitly destructive.

install-import-pickers-rule-31.rule: Per-target import mappers (custom `ImportEntryMapper`) MUST live in `<target>/import-mappers.ts` — never in `importer.ts`. Putting them in `importer.ts` and importing from `index.ts` forms a cycle: `index.ts → importer.ts → index.ts`, and the descriptor's object literal captures `undefined` for `map:` fields. Function references stored as descriptor fields are safe (live bindings); object literals capturing those references at module-init are not. Establish `import-mappers.ts` even for one mapper.

install-import-pickers-rule-32.rule: Don't migrate an `ignore` (or any single-output) feature to descriptor `flatFile` mode without re-reading the original importer. `flatFile` writes the FIRST `source` path verbatim — it never merges/dedupes. If the original concatenates multiple files (e.g. cursor merges `.cursorignore` + `.cursorindexingignore`), keep it imperative or extend the runner with `mergedFlatFile`.

install-import-pickers-rule-33.rule: `isLocalSource` for plugin paths must accept Windows drive-letter absolutes — match `/^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]/` alongside POSIX (`/…`, `./…`, `../…`, `file:`). Tests that build absolute paths with `resolve()` and feed them as plugin `source` exercise this.

install-import-pickers-rule-4.rule: Marketplace `--all` recursive installs must omit `--as` (only pass `--path` and `--target`) — `targetFromSubPack`'s first-feature inference forces the manual single-kind path which rejects mixed-content sub-packs.

install-import-pickers-rule-5.rule: Lower the picker's marketplace-branch threshold to `subPacks.length >= 1` when sub-packs come from explicit sources like `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. Singleton plugin lists must route through the marketplace branch, not `runSinglePackInstall` against an empty root. The directory-heuristic detector keeps its own `>= 2` floor.

install-import-pickers-rule-6.rule: Nested `runInstall` calls from picker auto-pick (single flat collection branch) MUST pass `replay ?? {}` as the 4th arg so the inner `if (replay === undefined)` guard skips `acquireInstallLock()` re-acquisition. Otherwise the inner call deadlocks against the outer's held lock.

install-import-pickers-rule-7.rule: `install --sync` replay must reapply persisted `features` + `pick` from `installs.yaml` before validation/selection (not just the saved path), must carry through the caller's `--force` and related validation flags (never hardcode `force: true`), and the replay parser must accept persisted internal source formats (`github:org/repo@sha`, `blob/...` URLs), not only user-entered URLs.

install-import-pickers-rule-8.rule: `install --sync --dry-run` is not provably side-effect free — validate in isolated temp projects or inspect the implementation before pointing it at a live workspace.

install-import-pickers-rule-9.rule: Persist manual single-item installs by **parent collection path + explicit `pick`**, never the discovered file path. Pack names must describe stable source identity + normalized install scope (not first-picked-item naming). For broader-than-one-path identity, persist aggregated `paths` and match packs by repo identity + feature set so sync replay across multiple folders of the same repo/feature works.

kilo-code-config-surface-for-kilo-code-c.rule: For kilo-code, current Kilo v7 (Kilo/OpenCode CLI) reads MCP under the `mcp` key inside `kilo.jsonc` (project `kilo.jsonc` or `.kilo/kilo.jsonc`; global `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc`) and reads `.kilo/rules/*.md` only when listed under the `instructions` key — `.kilo/mcp.json` + `mcpServers` wrapper and auto-loaded `.kilo/rules` are LEGACY (`.kilocode/`); generating to the new `.kilo/` layout without writing `mcp`/`instructions` keys produces files current Kilo will not load.

kilo-code-for-kilo-code-global-agents.rule: For kilo-code global agents, trust the dedicated custom-subagents.md doc page (plural ~/.config/kilo/agents/, stated 3x incl. Configuration Precedence) over custom-modes.md's singular ~/.config/kilo/agent/ (also stated 3x) — kilo.ai's own docs self-contradict on this path; custom-subagents.md is the newer CLI-focused page and is more authoritative.

lessons-a-new-lessons-subcommand-must.rule: A new lessons subcommand must also land in the renderer switch (src/cli/renderers/lessons.ts), the skill.ts subcommand list plus its canonical .agentsmesh/skills/lessons/SKILL.md and plugins/agentsmesh-lessons copies, the frozen-API golden, and CANONICAL_SUBCOMMANDS. lessons resolve shipped with no renderer case, so it printed nothing on success.

lessons-system-a-command-pattern-trigger.rationale: Conflating valid command_patterns with verified file-glob reachability overstates graph health.
lessons-system-a-command-pattern-trigger.rule: A command_pattern trigger's reachability cannot be verified statically the way a file_glob's can: a file_glob is dead/live against the working tree (deadFileGlobIds matches real files), but a command_pattern only has "compiles/valid" (isSafeRegexPattern) — there is no command corpus to test "matches a real command." Any lessons reachability/liveness audit MUST keep these tiers separate (file-reachable = verified vs the tree, command-pattern = valid-but-unverified), never sum them into one "reachable" bucket.

A command_pattern trigger's reachability cannot be verified statically the way a file_glob's can: a file_glob is judged against the working tree and git history (fileGlobLiveness in validate-liveness.ts), but a command_pattern only has 'compiles/valid' (isSafeRegexPattern); there is no command corpus to test 'matches a real command'. Any lessons reachability/liveness audit MUST keep these tiers separate (file-reachable = verified vs the tree, command-pattern = valid-but-unverified), never sum them into one 'reachable' bucket.

lessons-system-a-keyword-trigger-fires-o.rule: A keyword trigger fires ONLY when its full pattern is a substring of an explicit --keyword, OR its tokens appear as a CONTIGUOUS run inside the --file/--cmd tokens (keyword-match.ts: keywordMatches). Therefore a long descriptive keyword pattern (8+ tokens, e.g. 'antd Form.useForm getFieldsValue Select filterOption FormData generic cast') is effectively DEAD: it is never a substring of a realistic --keyword and never appears contiguously in a file path, so the lesson is reachable only via its file_glob. Author keyword triggers as SHORT distinctive runs (2-4 tokens, e.g. 'filterOption cast'). Proven empirically: long pattern returns (no matches) on a sibling file even with an on-topic --keyword; the short pattern matches.

lessons-system-a-non-backtracking-matche.rule: A non-backtracking matcher used in mandatory recall needs a QUERY-WIDE work budget shared across all triggers (per-pattern state caps are insufficient: N near-cap patterns sum to N×cost). Bound total NFA work, not input length — do NOT truncate input (truncation misses suffix matches and lets $ falsely match the invented endpoint); instead degrade a budget-exhausted match to a safe non-match. Also match new-RegExp(no-flags) exactly for the documented subset: . excludes \n \r U+2028 U+2029; \cX is a control char; reject (don't pass through) \xZZ-style and \c-non-letter rather than silently changing meaning.

lessons-system-a-plugin-only-distributio.rationale: The plugin path drops both the root paragraph and the hooks, leaving recall entirely discretionary.
lessons-system-a-plugin-only-distributio.rule: A plugin-only distribution silently loses the standing-instruction layer: a plugin cannot write CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, so the BLOCKING lessons paragraph that `init --lessons` puts in `.agentsmesh/rules/_root.md` never reaches the model, and a skill's name+description is only an advisory "use when" pointer. Carry the ritual in the MCP server's `instructions` field instead (`new Server({name,version},{capabilities},{instructions})` — optional in the SDK's InitializeResult, currently unset in src/mcp/server.ts). It reaches every MCP client at zero per-call cost, unlike hooks which pay a fresh npx resolution each invocation.

A plugin-only distribution silently loses the standing-instruction layer: a plugin ships skills, hooks and servers but never the user CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, so the BLOCKING lessons paragraph `init --lessons` writes into `.agentsmesh/rules/_root.md` never reaches the model, and a skill name+description is only an advisory "use when" pointer. Carry the ritual in the MCP server `instructions` field: it belongs in the SAME second options object as `capabilities` (`new Server({name,version},{capabilities,instructions})`), NOT a third argument. Assert it on the wire from the initialize result, not just on the constant, since the value is useless if the SDK does not serialize it.

lessons-system-a-skill-meant-as-a.rule: A skill meant as a fallback for an always-on rule MUST encode its binding triggers in the frontmatter description (the harness's discovery signal) — e.g. 'recall before every mutation, capture after every failure' — not merely 'consult when running X subcommands'. A reactive description only surfaces the skill once the agent already decided to use it, so it never fires proactively as the fallback; lead the description with the WHEN, then enumerate the how-to.

lessons-system-an-in-repo-non-backtracki.rule: An in-repo non-backtracking regex engine must: (a) use an ITERATIVE epsilon-closure — recursion overflows the stack on long ε-chains like (){1000}; (b) bound TOTAL expanded NFA state count (and matched input length), not just pattern length — a{1000} is 6 chars but ~2000 states and match cost is O(states×input); (c) decode \xHH and \uHHHH to their chars (and treat \b inside a class as backspace) to match new RegExp WITHOUT the u flag, not pass them through as literals.

evidence: workflow:wf_4a3a99d8-50d (confirmed blocker); fixed by threading RecallOptions.ttlMs and applying AUTO_SESSION_TTL_MS on the MCP path
lessons-system-any-recall-dedup-path-tha.rule: Any recall-dedup path that lacks a context-reset signal MUST bound suppression with a TTL. The hook resets on SessionStart compact/clear, so it needs none — but the MCP server (stdio, one long-lived process per client) never observes the client compacting, so an unbounded correlator hides a rule the client summarized away for the whole server lifetime, turning a BLOCKING recall gate into one that silently returns nothing. Pass ttlMs on every non-hook recall path (MCP, CLI --session auto) and keep a per-call escape (no_dedup / --no-dedup).

lessons-system-anything-the-recall-hook-.rule: Anything the recall hook derives from the outcome log runs before every edit and command: memoize per (lesson, action) and compute only for the lessons being ranked, then time the hook with a full 5000-event log. Unmemoized effectiveness added about 130 ms per hook call; memo plus scoping cut it to about 20 ms.

lessons-system-apply-the-same-legacy-aut.rule: Apply the same legacy auto-migration gate before every CLI and MCP lessons read or write so MCP capture cannot strand legacy lessons.

lessons-system-await-async-transaction-m.rule: Await async transaction mutators while holding the lessons lock, or reject Promise-returning mutators at runtime and in the public type contract.

lessons-system-before-adding-a-flag-name.rule: Before adding a flag name to the parser's valueless/boolean set (so it stops consuming the next token), confirm no command reads it as a value — e.g. --version is global-boolean for the CLI but value-taking for 'plugin add --version <ref>'/install pinning. Restrict the set to provably boolean-only globals (json, verbose, help).

lessons-system-before-turning-a-lessons-.rule: Before turning a lessons log on by default, re-run every consumer on the real log. The old effectiveness join reported 677 misses (65% on cmd:cd); counting a miss only for a failure in the same session, within 30 minutes, on an action the lesson's own trigger matches reports 4.

lessons-system-bound-compiled-nfa-size-a.rule: Bound compiled NFA size and command-match work, not only source-pattern length: bounded-repeat expansion can turn a short accepted command pattern into thousands of states and make mandatory recall exceed its latency budget.

lessons-system-call-a-lessons-file-glob.rule: Call a lessons file_glob that matches nothing on disk dead only with git proof: HEAD history deleted or renamed its path, and a wildcard glob needs a rename. Ignored build output, not-yet-created files, other branches and non-git projects stay pending and are never auto-detached; 'no match on disk' alone pruned live lessons on every fresh clone.

lessons-system-claude-code-posttoolusefa.rule: Claude Code PostToolUseFailure carries the failure text in a TOP-LEVEL `error` string whose first line is `Exit code N` (documented example: "error": "Exit code 1\nError: Cannot find module ..."), not in tool_error or tool_response. Read `error`, and class on the first line AFTER `Exit code N`, or every Bash failure collapses into one class. Before writing any hook payload extractor, copy the field names from the docs example JSON for that exact event and assert against a fixture built from it: an extractor built on a guessed field shipped and left 0 of 247 real failures classified for months.

lessons-system-claude-code-s-pretooluse-.rationale: A documented false belief drove the reactive PostToolUse-only design; the first touch was left unguarded.
lessons-system-claude-code-s-pretooluse-.rule: Claude Code's PreToolUse hook DOES support `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (inject context to the model BEFORE the tool runs) — verified against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks. This contradicts the old belief that PreToolUse can only gate (allow/deny/ask). So deterministic pre-edit recall is possible: a PreToolUse hook injects matching lessons before the FIRST touch, with no blocking and no permission interrupt (additionalContext is additive; absent permissionDecision the tool proceeds). Do not claim PreToolUse cannot inject context.

lessons-system-compile-command-pattern-t.rule: Compile command-pattern triggers at capture and validation boundaries; reject invalid regexes instead of silently making lessons unreachable.

lessons-system-copy-each-host-s-hook.rule: Copy each host's hook payload and answer shape from that host's docs: Copilot camelCase payloads have no hook_event_name (detect by sessionId plus source or toolName/error) and need exit code 2 on postToolUseFailure; Cursor answers with top-level additional_context and sends conversation_id (session_id only on sessionStart); Gemini's BeforeAgent is its prompt event. The CLI must pass the hook's exit code through: doHook hard-coded 0, so Copilot ignored the nudge.

lessons-system-differential-test-every-c.rule: Differential-test every claimed JavaScript-regex construct against new RegExp, including dot line terminators, dollar before a final newline, control escapes, classes, and long inputs; do not document full new RegExp semantics while accepted patterns can match differently.

lessons-system-do-not-add-a-two.rule: Do NOT add a two-token minimum floor to keyword-match derived-haystack matching (keyword-match.ts containsRun path). Distinctive single-token keyword triggers ('subagent', 'checkout') firing on file/command tokens is DELIBERATE — keyword-match.test.ts asserts it. Single-token false positives ('test','config') are handled at CAPTURE time by the LOW_SIGNAL_KEYWORD/STOPWORD guardrails, not by a match-time floor. General rule: several lessons-recall 'improvements' (broad-glob general type, keyword floor, stopword-haystack) contradict the deliberate precision design — verify against keyword-match.test.ts and the merge-graph precision lesson before changing matcher semantics.

lessons-system-do-not-claim-javascript-r.rule: Do not claim JavaScript regex command triggers are provably linear from local quantifier shape alone: unanchored patterns such as a+b can still rescan every start position and become quadratic. Require safe anchoring with a sound analyzer or use a linear-time regex engine.

lessons-system-do-not-export-a-raw.rule: Do not export a raw graph mutator as a stable ordinary-write API when it can strand legacy data; make it internal or require an explicit already-initialized capability, and route public writes through migration-aware application services.

lessons-system-do-not-silently-truncate-.rule: Do not silently truncate command input before regex matching: truncation creates false negatives for suffix matches and false positives for end-anchored patterns by inventing a new end-of-input. Preserve full semantics or explicitly reject over-budget queries.

lessons-system-do-not-treat-star-height.rule: Do not treat star-height-only regex analysis as a complete ReDoS guarantee; reject ambiguous repeated alternation, optional-overlap, and overlapping sequential quantifiers, or replace JavaScript regex command triggers with a provably linear matcher.

lessons-system-document-any-intentional-.rule: Document any intentional exception to lessons query token caps, such as always returning the top-ranked lesson even when it exceeds the cap.

lessons-system-don-t-assume-the-lessons.rule: Don't assume the lessons recall PostToolUse hook (agentsmesh lessons hook) fires after FAILED commands — Claude Code's PostToolUse is success-only; a non-zero-exit command routes to a separate PostToolUseFailure event (cannot block, shows stderr to Claude). So recall never runs post-failure, and a capture-on-failure nudge cannot ride PostToolUse; it would need PostToolUseFailure or a Stop hook. Verified against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.

lessons-system-enforce-an-effective-tota.rule: Enforce an effective total command-matcher work budget across states, input length, and trigger count: merely capping each NFA at 2000 states still lets one accepted near-cap pattern add multi-second latency to every mandatory recall.

lessons-system-enforce-the-content-addre.rule: Enforce the content-addressed trigger invariant in graph validation: reject duplicate (kind, pattern) trigger nodes so public mutations cannot bypass deduplication, fanout accounting, and ranking specificity.

lessons-system-ensure-a-public-first-wri.rule: Ensure a public first write cannot strand an existing legacy lessons store; migrate or reconcile legacy content under the same initialization lock before capture.

lessons-system-every-standalone-lessons-.rule: Every standalone lessons op that reads the graph (strip-markers, recall, any tryLoadLessonsGraph caller on a possibly-legacy project) must call maybeAutoMigrateLessons FIRST; tryLoadLessonsGraph alone returns null without migrating, so a legacy-only store is silently ignored.

lessons-system-exclude-interruptions-can.rule: Exclude interruptions, cancellations, and permission denials from mistake fingerprints; control-flow outcomes are not evidence of an agent mistake.

lessons-system-export-stable-error-class.rule: Export stable error classes thrown by public lessons APIs so callers can distinguish expected conflicts without depending on internal modules.

lessons-system-expose-a-high-level-lesso.rule: Expose a high-level lessons application API for recall, capture, and initialization that owns legacy migration, loading, ranking, and transactional writes; do not require public consumers to compose storage primitives correctly.

lessons-system-for-a-stranded-legacy-gra.rule: For a stranded legacy+graph state (legacy index.yaml coexisting with a populated lessons.json), provide non-destructive recovery: import-md --merge folds legacy lessons in via addLessonInto (rule-text dedup + content-addressed trigger dedup + topic union); a plain import must refuse and point at --merge (recover) vs --force (overwrite).

lessons-system-for-lesson-trigger-scope-.rationale: Supersedes lessons-system-when-reviewing-or-authoring-a: field usage showed keyword triggers near-useless for cross-file reach (concept vocab absent from file paths); file-class globs are the working recurrence-surface mechanism.
lessons-system-for-lesson-trigger-scope-.rule: For lesson-trigger scope, distinguish three kinds: a DISCOVERY-SITE pin (the single file a bug was found in — too narrow; it will NOT fire when the same general/library behavior recurs elsewhere), a FILE-CLASS glob (e.g. **/ui/*Selector*.tsx, **/lib/use*Form*.ts — the class of files where the behavior recurs; PRECISE and the correct recurrence surface for library/framework-behavior lessons), and a BROAD glob (src/** — HIGH_FANOUT noise, avoid). Trigger general/library-behavior lessons on the file-CLASS recurrence surface — NOT the discovery site, NOT a broad glob. Do NOT rely on keyword triggers for cross-file reach on the --file/--cmd path: a concept's vocabulary (labelInValue, useBlocker) rarely appears in the file paths where it recurs, so keyword triggers fire mainly on prompt text — the file-class glob is the reliable mechanism (production field evidence, 2026-07-05).

lessons-system-for-lessons-system-effici.rule: For lessons-system efficiency reviews, define the optimization metric as prevented repeat mistakes unless the user explicitly asks about runtime performance.

lessons-system-give-mandatory-lessons-re.rule: Give mandatory lessons recall a bounded default token budget or compact output mode; a count-only default limit can emit many long, weakly related rules and waste context.

lessons-system-implement-nfa-epsilon-ass.rule: Implement NFA epsilon/assertion closure iteratively and cap epsilon-chain/state depth: an accepted pattern containing repeated empty groups can overflow the recursive closure stack and make lessons query fail.

lessons-system-keep-every-lessons-implem.rule: Keep every lessons implementation file at or below the repository 200-line limit; split ranking helpers by responsibility before completion.

lessons-system-keep-lessons-reference-do.rule: Keep lessons reference documentation synchronized with actual exports, ranked recall semantics, validation codes, and write-lock guarantees.

lessons-system-keep-lessons-trigger-fano.rule: Keep lessons trigger fanout bounded and specific; treat HIGH_FANOUT_TRIGGERS validation warnings as a recall-precision and token-efficiency defect.

lessons-system-keep-mcp-tool-input-schem.rule: Keep MCP tool input schemas tolerant of and symmetric with the CLI surface. lessons_add originally required strict string[] arrays and only the plural field names, so CLI-muscle-memory calls (a bare string, or --trigger-file-style singular keys) hit VALIDATION_FAILED before the handler ran — while lessons_query already folded `cmd`/`max-tokens` aliases. Fix: accept string|string[] (z.union) and CLI-flag aliases in the schema, coerce in the handler mirroring CLI semantics exactly — triggers use repeatedFlag (scalar→[scalar], NEVER comma-split: globs/regexes contain commas), evidence uses listFlag (comma-split a scalar).

lessons-system-keep-the-nested-per-lesso.rule: Keep the nested per-lesson Map memo in action-match.ts: flattening it to one Map keyed by lessonId + separator + contextKey made effectiveness() on a 5000-event log about 50 ms instead of 20 ms (a new string per lookup on the recall hot path), and outcome-log lesson ids are not validated, so a separator key could clash.

lessons-system-key-a-failed-shell-comman.rule: Key a failed shell command on the segment that runs the real program: split on &&, ||, ; and | outside quotes, and skip cd, env assignments and known global flags (keying on the first word put 22 failures under cmd:cd). Build the capture trigger hint from the same class as \bprog\b.*\bsub\b, or it never matches the command that failed.

lessons-system-keyword-match-s-derived-h.rationale: Field evidence showed keyword recall near-useless because concept vocab is compressed into camelCase file identifiers; splitting sub-words (whole token retained) closes part of that gap without embeddings.
lessons-system-keyword-match-s-derived-h.rule: keyword-match's derived haystack (keyword-match.ts deriveHaystackTokens) now splits camelCase and ACRONYM→Word boundaries into sub-words WHILE retaining each identifier's whole lowercased token. So it stays backward compatible (whole-token matches still fire) and token-exact (no substring bleed — 'cat' still misses 'category'), but a distinctive sub-word keyword ('guard') now reaches camelCase-named files ('useLeaveGuard.ts'). It does NOT split lowercase-joined identifiers ('readonly'). When changing matcher semantics, retain the whole token for backward compatibility, keep it token-exact (no floor, no substring), and verify against keyword-match.test.ts.

lessons-system-lesson-coverage-checks-ho.rationale: Two independent review agents flagged the raw-vs-normalized asymmetry as a bug and recommended normalizing the coverage query, which would break command_pattern coverage.
lessons-system-lesson-coverage-checks-ho.rule: Lesson COVERAGE checks (hook.ts hasCoveringLesson) must query with the RAW command, NOT the normalized contextKey class. A command_pattern trigger is a regex matched against the FULL command, so normalizing 'git commit -m x' to the class 'git commit' makes a trigger like /git commit -m/ miss → false 'uncovered' escalations. The asymmetry is deliberate: the recurrence KEY (contextKey/normalizeCommand) normalizes to GROUP failures by action; the coverage QUERY uses the raw command to MATCH triggers accurately. Do not "fix" this into consistency.

lessons-system-lessons-split-by-reach-na.rule: Lessons split by REACH: named-conceptual (concept appears in the task text → keyword trigger + UserPromptSubmit recall); scoped (file_glob/command_pattern); and AMBIENT/universal — applies to every task but is named by NO query (e.g. 'comment style' on prompt 'add a feature'). No query-based recall (keyword OR semantic) can surface an ambient lesson, so it needs scope:'always' (graph-tracked, no trigger, delivered on every task via the UserPromptSubmit hook + 'lessons query --always'). scope:'always' is DISTINCT from a broad file_glob (still forbidden — dilutes triggered precision): it is not matched at all, just always delivered. lessons-system-make-a-bounded-file-walk.rule: Make a bounded file walk return null (unknown) when it hits its cap, never the partial list: a 'no match' verdict over a partial list marks live globs dead.

lessons-system-make-public-graph-mutatio.rule: Make public graph mutation helpers migrate before any pre-read early return; stripMarkersInGraph currently returns no-op on a legacy-only store instead of migrating and applying the requested mutation.

lessons-system-make-public-legacy-import.rule: Make public legacy import refuse an existing lessons graph by default and require explicit overwrite intent inside the locked transaction.

lessons-system-mark-recalled-lessons-as-.rule: Mark recalled lessons as seen only after every output cap is applied: the CLI renderer cut rules past 32,000 characters after dedup had committed them, so with --session they were never delivered. Trim to the printed payload in the handler, before commitSeen.

lessons-system-merge-a-lesson-s-list.rule: Merge a lesson's list fields (triggers, topics, evidence) as base-aware sets in the three-way merge; taking one side's whole record silently drops the other side's triggers and evidence.

lessons-system-never-compile-an-author-s.rule: Never compile an author-supplied lessons file_glob with picomatch on any path: recall, validate, prune, capture guardrails or effectiveness. picomatch passes (…), | and +-after-) through as a backtracking regex even with noextglob, and the synchronous hang cannot be stopped by a test timeout. Use getGlobMatcher from src/lessons/glob-safety.ts and treat null as never matching.

lessons-system-never-configure-a-git-mer.rule: Never configure a git merge driver whose program is not on PATH: git cannot start it, keeps %A as it is with no conflict markers, and the next git add silently drops the other branch's lessons. Check the launcher exists first and report the setup as failed.

lessons-system-never-infer-that-a-recall.rule: Never infer that a recalled lesson failed from a tool failure alone; require an exact durable mistake-to-lesson evidence link before prompting lesson review.

lessons-system-never-limit-a-git-log.rule: Never limit a git log -M rename scan with a pathspec: a rename whose new path is outside the pathspec is reported as a plain delete, so a renamed file looks deleted.

lessons-system-never-swap-merge-code-s.rule: Never swap merge code's version-1 empty graph (absentGraph in merge-sides.ts) for emptyGraph(): emptyGraph() stamps CURRENT_GRAPH_VERSION and mergeGraphs keeps the higher version, so an absent side would silently upgrade a v1 graph on merge.

lessons-system-preserve-documented-regex.rule: Preserve documented regex semantics in the linear command matcher: reject invalid JavaScript-regex syntax and either implement or explicitly reject every unsupported escape or assertion instead of accepting it with a different meaning.

lessons-system-preserve-every-occurrence.rule: Preserve every occurrence of repeatable CLI flags in the shared argument parser; do not overwrite earlier trigger values.

lessons-system-provide-a-lossless-reconc.rule: Provide a lossless reconciliation path when legacy index.yaml and a populated lessons.json coexist; auto-migration currently skips forever, while import without force refuses and force overwrites fresh graph content.

lessons-system-re-export-every-error-cla.rule: Re-export every error class a public function is documented to throw (e.g. LessonsGraphExistsError) from the package public surface, so consumers can catch it via instanceof rather than string-matching messages.

lessons-system-re-run-line-counts-after.rule: Re-run line counts after every lessons matcher change and split helpers before completion; adding semantic support pushed regex-linear/parse.ts beyond the repository's blocking 200-line maximum.

lessons-system-read-stdout-stderr-or-a.rule: Read stdout, stderr or a string tool_response as failure text only when the hook payload carries a failure signal; success events carry output too, and reading it unconditionally records successful commands as failures.

lessons-system-redos-protection-for-user.rule: ReDoS protection for user-supplied regexes executed on a hot path (e.g. lessons command_pattern recall) MUST fail closed: accept only a provably-linear subset and reject everything else. Heuristic "detect the unsafe shape" approaches (star-height / nested-repetition detectors) fail open — bypasses include (a|aa)+, (a|a?)+, and a+a+ (no nested repetition, still catastrophic). Either run a linear engine (RE2) or allowlist-reject quantified groups, adjacent repetition, backreferences, and lookarounds.

lessons-system-reject-duplicate-ids-with.rule: Reject duplicate ids within each lesson's topics and triggers arrays, and duplicate evidence entries if evidence is set-like; duplicate trigger references currently persist and distort fanout and specificity ranking.

lessons-system-reject-or-safely-execute-.rule: Reject or safely execute command_pattern regexes with catastrophic-backtracking risk; syntax-valid user-controlled patterns must not be able to hang mandatory lessons recall.

lessons-system-route-every-lessons-graph.rule: Route every lessons graph writer, including migration and scaffolding, through the shared locked transaction path.

Bound every signal-less correlator three ways: reset the whole session on an idle gap (a pause means the old chat ended), cap each entry with a short TTL, and — where the harness reports it — clear on SessionStart `startup` (new chat) while leaving `resume` alone. There is no generate-time always-block (no renderAlwaysLessonsBlock, no lessons-always.ts); a static digest baked into _root.md was rejected because it cannot be complete, bounded and current at once.

lessons-system-session-recall-dedup-seen.rule: Session recall dedup (seen-cache) assumes a delivered lesson STAYS in the model's context — but a long chat gets compacted/summarized and can drop it, while dedup (keyed by session_id, which survives compaction) keeps suppressing it: the two desync and the lesson is lost. Tie dedup to the CONTEXT lifecycle, not the wall clock: on SessionStart source 'compact'/'clear' (Claude Code fires this; source in startup|resume|clear|compact), clearSeen() so the next recall re-injects. startup/resume KEEP the set (resume restores prior context). A blind TTL only approximates this — SessionStart(compact) is the exact signal.

lessons-system-the-recall-hook-hook-ts.rule: The recall hook (hook.ts) detects a tool FAILURE by EITHER hook_event_name==='PostToolUseFailure' OR a non-empty tool_error in the payload — so failure recording is portable to harnesses that signal errors on a normally-named tool-call event, not just Claude Code's dedicated failure event. Do NOT build a static preload digest baked into _root.md: a query-less static block cannot be complete AND bounded AND relevant (a token cap silently drops the tail on a large graph), goes stale between init runs, and is redundant on hook targets. lessons-system-treat-each-repeated-trigg.rule: Treat each repeated trigger flag as one opaque value; never split regex or glob patterns on commas.

lessons-system-when-a-lexical-or-bm25.rule: When a lexical or BM25 candidate gate counts shared terms, exclude generic English words (top, left, before, first, new, use, ...) from the count even though they are not stopwords for scoring: a two-term overlap gate on raw tokens qualified a merge-conflict-marker rule for an SVG prompt on 'top' and 'left'. Let IDF weigh such words in the score, but never let them be the reason a rule qualifies.
