lessons-telemetry-when-interpreting-less.rule: When interpreting `lessons stats`, diagnose deployment before content: intra-session redundancy above ~25% combined with sessions counted by time-gap means NO session correlator reaches recall (harness hook stdin absent, or the CLI ritual run without --session) — dedup is inert and most "skimming noise" is repeats; a high no-match rate (with returned-token p50≈0) is normally the unconditional per-command recall against a graph with few command_pattern triggers — a latency cost, not a token cost. Fix those two before touching ranking or rule content.

lessons-the-lessons-graph-has-no.rule: The lessons graph has NO generated JSON Schema in schemas/; it is validated only by the in-code Zod LessonsGraphSchema (src/lessons/graph-schema.ts) and is deliberately excluded from buildAllSchemas/generate-schemas.ts — for a graph-schema contract golden, mint it from z.toJSONSchema(LessonsGraphSchema), do not look for a schemas/lessons.json file.

link-rebaser-deterministic-text-cleanup-.rationale: strip-markers' cosmetic cleanup regex mangled code samples in 11 lessons; caught only by corpus verification, not unit tests.
link-rebaser-deterministic-text-cleanup-.rule: Deterministic text-cleanup transforms over rule/doc prose that embeds code samples MUST be deletion-only — never reflow whitespace or punctuation. A cosmetic `replace(/\s+([,.;:])/g, '$1')` or multi-space collapse corrupts embedded code: `${{ ... }}` → `${{... }}`, `exit 1 ;;` → `exit 1;;`, `[ref]: ...` → `[ref]:...`. To strip a trailing marker that owns its terminal period, make the period part of the marker's own regex match (e.g. `\bSee\s+L\d+\.?`) instead of post-collapsing `..` afterward. Verify any prose transform against the real corpus and assert ellipses/fences/shell-punctuation survive byte-for-byte.

link-rebaser-never-leave-a-scratch-deliv.rule: Never leave a scratch/delivery file at the repo root whose basename matches a canonical artifact (e.g. lessons.json): the reference rewriter is project-root-relative and existence-gated, so 'agentsmesh generate' resolves canonical paths like .agentsmesh/lessons/lessons.json down to the root lessons.json and silently rewrites every generated root-instruction file (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .goosehints, ...). Use a non-colliding name (lessons.fixed.json) or write outside the repo, then re-run generate.

link-rebaser-rule-1.rule: Treat reference-style Markdown definitions (`[ref]: ...`, titled, angle-bracketed) as link destinations, not prose anchors — apply the same destination-relative rewrite contract as inline links.

link-rebaser-rule-10.rule: Preserve/add `./` prefix for same-directory descendant links inside generated Markdown (`formatLinkPathForDestination`). Assert the exact rendered path (`./skills/post-feature-qa/`) in tests, never "not canonical" loose matches.

link-rebaser-rule-11.rule: URI-skip patterns (`ssh://`, `git@host:`) must keep the scheme matcher distinct from Windows drive-letter detection — never let a single-letter scheme regex swallow `C:` and block legitimate absolute paths. Add same-file regression for both.

link-rebaser-rule-12.rule: Path tokenizers must require enough structure to distinguish file references from prose markers — the absolute-path branch must NOT match a bare `/` (e.g. `✓ / ✗` status text).

link-rebaser-rule-13.rule: Inline backtick path rewrites: tests asserting the rewritten form must accept any of `` `docs/...` ``, `` `/docs/...` ``, `` `./docs/...` ``, `` `../docs/...` `` via a permissive regex — Windows 8.3-shortname realpath divergence makes the exact form non-deterministic. The contract is "stable destination," not "always project-root-relative."

link-rebaser-rule-14.rule: `expandResolvedPaths` must yield the caller's `projectRoot`-shaped path FIRST, then the realpath variant as a tie-breaker — never `unshift(realPath)`. Realpath-first breaks `toProjectRootRelative` on DOS short names (`RUNNER~1` vs `runneradmin`) and symlinked tmpdirs. Audit every `[realpath, original]` loop.

link-rebaser-rule-15.rule: Import normalization must include BOTH the direct joined target path AND its `realpathSync.native` variant in the lookup map. Temp-workspace runs resolve through realpath and otherwise stay target-specific after import.

link-rebaser-rule-16.rule: Import normalization must build the rewrite map from every supported generated path family across ALL targets, not just the source target — re-importing a polluted artifact must recover canonical `.agentsmesh/...` links cross-family.

link-rebaser-rule-17.rule: Do not normalize bare root filenames (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `GEMINI.md`) as raw substrings on the import side — they are common standalone words in prose. Only normalize when they appear in a structured path form.

link-rebaser-rule-18.rule: Any code participating in the link-rewrite map (key construction OR lookup) MUST use `pathApi(projectRoot)` from `src/core/path-helpers.ts`. NEVER import `join`/`normalize` from `node:path` directly in `src/core/reference/` or target-side `applyXxxRefs` helpers.

link-rebaser-rule-19.rule: Unit tests using a synthetic POSIX root (e.g. `ROOT = '/proj'`) with link-rewrite map machinery must alias `join`/`normalize` to `posix.join`/`posix.normalize` from `node:path/posix` — host `node:path` is win32 on Windows runners and silently mismatches the map.

link-rebaser-rule-2.rule: Preserve well-known canonical tokens (e.g. `.agentsmesh/`) in prose/labels/quoted/reading-context positions, but rewrite real Markdown inline-link destinations cross-format. Audit prose vs link classifier whenever formatter semantics change.

link-rebaser-rule-20.rule: After extracting helpers from `link-rebaser.ts` (e.g. `normalizeSeparators`, formatter helpers), scan every remaining branch (especially preservation/protected paths) for moved symbols and rerun the narrowest affected suite BEFORE expanding verification.

link-rebaser-rule-21.rule: Whenever the link-rewriter protection contract changes (fenced code, inline backticks, URI skips, drive letters), update both the main rewrite tests AND `link-rebaser-edge-cases.test.ts` in the same pass — the edge-case suite codifies the same contract separately.

link-rebaser-rule-22.rule: Reference-rewrite audits must search REAL canonical content for path patterns (including directory-form refs like `.agentsmesh/skills/post-feature-qa/`) and add tests for both exact files AND directory-form references. Synthetic round trips are insufficient — regenerate live target artifacts and grep the exact reported pattern.

link-rebaser-rule-23.rule: Generated Markdown demo content must use link destinations that resolve from EVERY generated target folder after rebasing. Keep speculative project-root examples as prose, not as clickable Markdown destinations.

link-rebaser-rule-24.rule: When parsing inline-link destinations with regex captures (e.g. `parseMarkdownLinkDestination`), guard the specific capture explicitly (`match?.[1] !== undefined`) under strict indexed access — don't rely on regex structure.

link-rebaser-rule-25.rule: Before adding extension-level skip gates in `rewriteGeneratedReferences()`, inspect the reference-rewrite matrix — supporting files like `template.ts` comments must still be rewritten; only token/comment-aware logic, not a blanket non-Markdown skip.

link-rebaser-rule-26.rule: Strict-prose assertions ("no leftover canonical mesh path") must run on prose with ALL rewriter-protected tokens stripped (fenced code, external refs, AND Windows absolute path tokens `/[A-Za-z]:[\\/][^\s,<>"'+'`'+`]+/`). The `WINDOWS_ABSOLUTE_PATH` guard in `link-rebaser.ts` is by-design.

link-rebaser-rule-27.rule: `shouldRewritePathToken` must split quote-like wrappers by intent: backticks (`` ` ``) are inline code and rewrite; single (`'`) and double (`"`) quotes are string-literal contexts inside code-like prose and stay verbatim. Don't restore the three-wrapper conflation in `link-token-context.ts`. When a canonical script needs a sibling file, author `Path(__file__).parent / "sibling.py"`, not `Path(__file__).parent / ".agentsmesh/skills/.../sibling.py"` — relying on the rebaser to "fix" the latter is the masking pattern this rule retires.

link-rebaser-rule-3.rule: Never inline `.agentsmesh/` as an exact substring in generated root-instruction decoration prose — reference-rewrite e2e strips fenced code and asserts the substring is gone. Phrase as ``the `.agentsmesh` directory at the project root``. Strip both old and new contract blocks on import.

link-rebaser-rule-4.rule: Add every emitted artifact path (including `additionalRootDecorationPaths`, multi-output families like Copilot's `.github/copilot/*.instructions.md` + `.github/instructions/*.md`, and Windsurf shared `AGENTS.md`) to the generate-side output-source map and build rewrite maps per output path / artifact family, not just per target.

link-rebaser-rule-5.rule: Pack skill artifact paths (`.agentsmesh/packs/.../skills/...`) must be added to `buildArtifactPathMap` alongside canonical `.agentsmesh/skills/...` so the rebaser translates both canonical and pack absolute paths.

link-rebaser-rule-6.rule: Shared artifact collision must compare canonicalized (un-rewritten) content, not post-rewrite bytes — collapse target-specific rewritten links back to canonical before declaring a true conflict. Keep target-native rewrite probes in protected fenced blocks or target-filtered fixtures so they don't poison shared outputs.

link-rebaser-rule-7.rule: Existence-gate rewriting: classify "should rewrite" vs "should stay unchanged because resolution fails" explicitly. Don't blindly normalize relative-looking refs whose targets don't exist (e.g. missing checklist refs, fixture `../SKILL.md`). Audit both categories whenever the link contract changes.

link-rebaser-rule-8.rule: For bare multi-segment paths under a root-relative contract (`src/AGENTS.md`, `docs/...`), resolve from the project root first, fall back to source-relative only if the root candidate is invalid. Add nested-file regression tests.

link-rebaser-rule-9.rule: For `../` over-traversal that escapes the workspace, retry resolution from the project root before giving up — real canonical files contain `../../../../docs/...` that still mean repo-root files. Cover in unit + all-target generate/import matrices.

lock-file-format-src-config-core-lock-ts.rule: src/config/core/lock.ts sits ~199 lines against the 200-line cap. When adding a LockFile field that round-trips through readLock/writeLock, put all new drift/build logic in a sibling file (e.g. lock-outputs.ts) and keep lock.ts edits to minimal parse/serialize lines; trim adjacent comments if you spill past 200.

lock-file-format-src-config-core-lock-ts.rationale: Issue #98 fix initially hashed raw GenerateResult.content while writeFileAtomic normalized line endings on write — any CRLF content would self-report as drift immediately after generate; caught in final review.
lock-file-format-src-config-core-lock-ts.rule: When recording or comparing checksums of files written via writeFileAtomic, hash the normalized payload (mirror hashFileForManifest: strip UTF-8 BOM + LF-normalize for shouldNormalizeLineEndings extensions, raw bytes otherwise) — never hash raw in-memory content, since writeFileAtomic rewrites CRLF to LF on disk and the hashes diverge.

mcp-generate-lock-the-mcp-generate-handl.rationale: MCP generate wrote target files but not .agentsmesh/.lock while returning lockfileUpdated:true; routing through runGenerate fixed it.
mcp-generate-lock-the-mcp-generate-handl.rule: The MCP generate handler (src/mcp/handlers/orchestrate.ts) MUST delegate to the CLI runGenerate, never reimplement file-writing — a bespoke reimplementation silently skips the lockfile write, stale-output cleanup, and process lock that `agentsmesh generate` guarantees, leaving `check` permanently drifted.

mcp-path-containment-mcp-path-containmen.rule: MCP path containment: canonicalize() reconstructs a DANGLING symlink leaf (a link whose target does not exist) as if it were an in-root file — realpath throws ENOENT, the tail is re-appended, and assertContainedPath then ALLOWS it. Any writer relying on the guard MUST create via temp-file + rename (rename replaces the link) and must NEVER writeFile directly on the target path (that follows the dangling link and writes outside the project). safeWrite/safeConfigWrite/atomicWrite are all rename-based; keep every new MCP writer rename-based.

MCP path containment must anchor the boundary at the PROJECT ROOT, never at `.agentsmesh`: a `.agentsmesh` boundary canonicalizes THROUGH a symlinked `.agentsmesh` and cancels (root and boundary both resolve outside, so the escape passes) — this lets a symlinked `.agentsmesh` parent leak reads and land destructive out-of-tree writes. Guard EVERY user/config read, write, AND delete at choke points so no handler can forget: canonical `list` (not just get/update/delete), settings config WRITES (atomicWrite + safeConfigWrite), and read-before-write pre-reads (updatePermissions/updateIgnore append). Every symlink test must `it.skipIf(platform()==='win32')` — unprivileged Windows `symlink()` throws EPERM and reddens the windows-latest CI matrix.

mcp-path-containment-mutate-raw-mcp-docu.rule: Mutate raw MCP documents rather than lossy normalized projections; reject malformed or unreadable existing documents and preserve every untouched server and top-level field.

mcp-path-containment-validate-every-skil.rule: Validate every skill mutation path and body size before the first write; reject the primary SKILL.md as a supporting-file mutation, including case variants, so validation failures cannot leave partial changes.

pnpm-lockfile-in-this-repo-run-dev.rule: In this repo, run dev tooling via `node_modules/.bin/<tool>` (vitest, tsup, tsx, changeset) — NOT `pnpm <script>` / `pnpm exec`. Any pnpm-11 invocation runs a deps-status-check that strips the pnpm-10 `hono` override from `pnpm-lock.yaml`, re-breaking CI's `--frozen-lockfile`. After build/test/changeset runs, check `git status`; if `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.agentsmesh/.lock` (timestamp-only), or `tests/e2e/agents-last-run.md` show as modified, `git checkout -- <them>` before committing — they are spurious churn.

pnpm-lockfile-pnpm-overrides-live-in-thr.rule: pnpm overrides live in THREE synced places: `package.json` `pnpm.overrides`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `overrides`, and the `pnpm-lock.yaml` `overrides:` snapshot. When adding/changing an override, update all three — edit both config files, then regenerate the lock with the CI pnpm major (`CI=true npx -y pnpm@10 install --lockfile-only`) and confirm `CI=true npx -y pnpm@10 install --frozen-lockfile` exits 0. Editing only `package.json` (as a lone security-override commit does) leaves `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and the lockfile snapshot stale and breaks CI's frozen install with ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH.

pnpm-lockfile-the-committed-pnpm-lock-ya.rationale: CI frozen install failed because package.json's hono override was missing from the lockfile; local pnpm 11 reported the lockfile up-to-date and would not add it, so the fix required regenerating with pnpm 10.
pnpm-lockfile-the-committed-pnpm-lock-ya.rule: The committed `pnpm-lock.yaml` `overrides:` block must match `package.json` `pnpm.overrides` exactly, or CI's `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails with ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH. CI runs pnpm 10 (pinned via `pnpm/action-setup` `version: 10`); local pnpm 11 will NOT repair the mismatch — `pnpm install --lockfile-only` reports "Already up to date" and leaves the overrides snapshot stale. Regenerate with the CI major and verify with it: `CI=true npx -y pnpm@10 install --lockfile-only` then `CI=true npx -y pnpm@10 install --frozen-lockfile` must exit 0 before committing.

process-locks-fail-on-stale-lock-evictio.rule: Fail on stale-lock eviction errors instead of retrying indefinitely; remove an incomplete lock when holder metadata cannot be written, without masking the original filesystem error.

process-locks-never-delete-a-process-loc.rule: Never delete a process lock by path after judging its holder stale: another process may take the lock between the judgement and the delete. Remove only your exact owner-<token> marker, tear down only after winning that removal, and delete holder.json only when its token matches.

process-locks-when-wiring-any-process-lo.rule: When wiring any process lock through acquireProcessLock (a new *-lock.ts wrapper or an inline call), pass a human-readable label (e.g. 'lessons lock', 'install lock') in LockOptions — LockAcquisitionError builds its message from that label and silently defaults to a generic 'lock', so a forgotten label mislabels the lock in the contention error without failing any test.

When wiring any process lock through acquireProcessLock (a new *-lock.ts wrapper or an inline call), pass a human-readable label (e.g. 'lessons lock', 'install lock') in LockOptions — LockAcquisitionError builds its message from that label and silently defaults to a generic 'lock', so a forgotten label mislabels the lock in the contention error without failing any test.

readme-authoring-before-publishing-any-c.rule: Before publishing any competitor comparison (README 'How AgentsMesh compares', website reference/alternatives.mdx), re-verify every row against the competitor's SOURCE, not a prior summary: as of 2026-09-19 rulesync ships a self-serve MCP server (src/cli/commands/mcp.ts + src/mcp/) and a documented programmatic API with a global --json envelope, both of which our table wrongly marked absent/partial, and neither rulesync nor Ruler advertises a tool count so quoting 'their marketing number' invented a claim. Verified-unique rows are cross-file link rewriting, lockfile-verified drift + merge recovery, target plugins, and lessons.

readme-authoring-before-publishing-readm.rule: Before publishing README, website, or marketing copy that claims 'safe adoption', 'lossless import', or 'nothing overwritten blind', run the two-root-file repro (repo with both CLAUDE.md and .cursor/rules/*.mdc, then 'init --yes' or two sequential 'import --from'): as of v0.38.0 the second import silently overwrites .agentsmesh/rules/_root.md and reports success for both, so the claim is false for the most common adopter. Verify the fix landed, or soften the claim, before shipping the copy.

readme-authoring-when-trimming-or-rewrit.rationale: User correction: a lean rewrite dropped the init wizard and auto link rebasing; the user had to ask for a deep feature re-check and a second rewrite.
readme-authoring-when-trimming-or-rewrit.rule: When trimming or rewriting README.md, do not sacrifice feature coverage for brevity. Cross-check the rewrite against the actual feature set (website/src/content/docs/** and src/cli/help-data.ts) and keep the differentiators — especially the `init` interactive wizard (targets → import → lessons → generate) and automatic link rebasing (canonical refs like `.agentsmesh/skills/.../x` rewritten to each target's native path). The readme skill's "lean" default must not silently drop recently-added or distinguishing features.

readme-codegen-blocks-when-trimming-or-r.rationale: A README cleanup can delete the wide matrix tables as "clutter", which breaks matrix:generate (throws on missing markers) and matrix-docs.test.ts (pins the first |Feature| table + exact global-scope heading).
readme-codegen-blocks-when-trimming-or-r.rule: When trimming or rewriting README.md, preserve the auto-generated marker blocks `<!-- agentsmesh:support-matrix:project -->`, `<!-- agentsmesh:support-matrix:global -->`, and `<!-- agentsmesh:tool-list -->`; keep the exact heading `### Global scope (`agentsmesh generate --global`)` directly above the global matrix; and keep the project matrix as the FIRST `| Feature ` table (give other tables a different first column, e.g. `| Command |`). `scripts/render-support-matrix.ts` throws on missing matrix markers and `tests/unit/core/matrix-docs.test.ts` pins this layout — finish with `pnpm matrix:generate && pnpm matrix:verify`.

reference-rewriting-when-a-target-genera.rule: When a target generates MULTIPLE canonical agents into ONE combined output file (e.g. cline .cline/agents.yaml), audit the whole reference-rewrite chain: buildReferenceMap must skip the many-to-one prose mapping (else all agent references rewrite to the combined file and cannot round-trip), buildOutputSourceMap needs an explicit fallback entry so command/rule/skill refs inside the combined file still rewrite, and the target's import-map builder must parse the combined file to emit per-agent canonical mappings.

reference-rewriting-when-a-target-s-gene.rationale: Amazon Q deniedPaths cannot express `!re-inclusion` or comments; a wholesale writeFileAtomic on .agentsmesh/ignore destroyed them for claude-code/aider/cursor too.
reference-rewriting-when-a-target-s-gene.rule: When a target's generate projection is lossy (drops comments, negations, or per-scope structure), the importer MUST merge into the existing canonical file instead of overwriting it — preserve every line the target cannot represent, or the next import silently deletes canonical data every other target still reads.

release-changesets-after-merging-master-.rule: After merging master into develop following a release, run `tsx scripts/sync-release-versions.ts` and commit before anything else: the version PR bumps package.json and server.json on master, but plugins/agentsmesh-lessons/*.json exist only on develop and keep the old version, so tests/unit/package/plugin-bundle.test.ts fails until the sync runs. The failure is the guard working, not a regression.

release-changesets-during-release-prep-r.rationale: The CI job runs this exact command; a masked exit code turns a red release into a surprise CI failure after push.
release-changesets-during-release-prep-r.rule: During release prep, run `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high` as its own command and read the real exit code — never pipe it through `tail`/`grep`, which reports the filter's status and hides a failing gate. Re-run it even when a dependency was bumped for advisories recently: new CVEs land against already-patched versions (tar 7.5.20 was clean at bump time, then GHSA-r292-9mhp-454m required >=7.5.21).

release-changesets-to-make-a-step-run.rule: To make a step run during `changeset version`, pass `version: pnpm run version` to changesets/action@v1 — it defaults to a bare `changeset version` and never invokes the package.json script. Input names differ by major: v1 uses publish/version/title/commit, the current README documents publish-script/version-script.

release-changesets-when-auditing-which-c.rationale: A release audit found a feat(skills) commit that needed no changeset (repo-internal only) and an unlabeled MCP bug fix that did — classification hinges on the npm files surface.
release-changesets-when-auditing-which-c.rule: When auditing which changes since the last release tag need a changeset, only the npm-published surface is user-facing: `src/`, `schemas/`, `package.json` (deps/exports), and `README.md` (the package `files` field is dist/schemas/README.md/CHANGELOG.md/LICENSE). Changes confined to `.agentsmesh/`, `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `tests/`, `website/`, or `docs/` ship nothing and need NO changeset — even a `feat(...)`-prefixed commit (e.g. adding a repo-internal skill). Enumerate with `git log v<last-tag>..HEAD --no-merges` and map every user-facing commit to a changeset.

security-a-directory-reader-that-ingests.rule: A directory reader that ingests untrusted native/pack content into canonical or a redistributable pack must not follow escaping symlinks; when hardening one reader (e.g. the canonical rules/commands/agents parsers), fix EVERY sibling reader — the native import readers (import-orchestrator, skill-import-pipeline, target-native-commands, per-target importers) share the exact same exfiltration class, so half-fixing leaves host-secret exfiltration open. For untrusted git clones also set core.symlinks=false.

security-resolve-existing-parent-directo.rule: Resolve existing parent directories against the real project root before generated writes or stale deletion; validate managed directories before traversal. Preserve internal directory symlinks and replace or unlink leaf symlinks without following them.

security-the-extends-elevated-artifact-g.rationale: Adding the default-strip consent gate to the shared extends load path changed existing tests that relied on remote extends merging elevated artifacts; future edits must keep that coupling in mind.
security-the-extends-elevated-artifact-g.rule: The extends elevated-artifact gate (`gateExtendElevatedArtifacts` in src/canonical/extends/, applied inside `loadCanonicalWithExtends`) strips hooks/permissions/mcp from REMOTE extends (github/gitlab/git, incl. git+file://) by default; only `accept: [...]` on the entry keeps them, and LOCAL extends are trusted as-is. When changing this gate, the remote-extend tests that supply elevated artifacts via git+file:// — tests/e2e/multi-extend-precedence.e2e.test.ts, tests/e2e/extends-remote.e2e.test.ts, tests/integration/extends.integration.test.ts — depend on `accept:` on the remote entry and silently lose those artifacts (changed assertions) without it.

security-use-exclusive-temporary-files-p.rule: Use exclusive temporary files per atomic write; preserve unrelated siblings and the original destination on failure, set permissions before rename, and ignore new lock-temp names in watchers.

security-when-hardening-a-git-spawn.rule: When hardening a git spawn site against SSRF/redirect (assertAllowedGitUrl + GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL), apply the SAME guard to ALL git spawn runners — the clone runner in src/config/remote/git-remote.ts, not just ls-remote in src/install/source/git-pin.ts. String-level parseGitSource validation does not constrain server-side redirects during clone.

security-when-hardening-git-transport-se.rule: When hardening git transport security, apply the protocol allowlist (assertAllowedGitUrl) AND GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL to BOTH spawn sites — the ls-remote/ref-resolution runner (git-pin.ts) and the clone runner (git-remote.ts) — and set core.symlinks=false on clone; hardening only ls-remote leaves redirect-during-clone (https->ext:: RCE, file:// read) reachable.

shell-quoting-construct-control-characte.rule: Construct control-character values directly in inline Node probes; do not interpolate raw control bytes into a JSON string and JSON.parse it, because raw line/control characters make the probe fail before testing the product.

shell-quoting-for-inline-typescript-eval.rule: For inline TypeScript eval scripts that need await, wrap the body in an async IIFE unless the runner is explicitly configured for ESM output.

shell-quoting-in-zsh-bash-calls-never.rationale: A chained cat/echo command failed with "==== not found", silently dropping two file reads and costing a round-trip.
shell-quoting-in-zsh-bash-calls-never.rule: In zsh Bash calls, never use a bare `=====` (or any token starting with `=`) as an echo separator between chained commands; zsh expands `=word` as an equals-expansion and aborts the whole chain. Quote it ('-----') or use plain dashes.

shell-quoting-in-zsh-bash-calls-never-2.rule: In zsh Bash calls, never keep a command or a list of paths in one variable and expand it unquoted: zsh does not word-split, so C='node dist/cli.js'; $C runs a command literally named 'node dist/cli.js' (command not found, easily hidden by a grep), and prettier $files receives one giant path (ENAMETOOLONG). Use a shell function, an array, or xargs.

shell-quoting-never-delete-a-ts-function.rule: Never delete a TS function with a regex whose optional leading doc-comment group is `(/\*\*[\s\S]*?\*/\n)?` — the lazy inner match still spans MULTIPLE comments, so the engine extends group 1 from the file-header comment all the way down to the comment above the target function and deletes every import in between. It fails loudly only if a later step reads the imports; otherwise it silently guts the file. Delete code blocks line-based instead: find the line starting `async function <name>(`, walk back over an immediately-preceding comment block, walk forward to a column-0 `}`.

shell-quoting-never-insert-zero-width-or.rationale: A zero-width space used to avoid closing a JSDoc block comment failed pnpm lint (no-irregular-whitespace).
shell-quoting-never-insert-zero-width-or.rule: Never insert zero-width or other irregular whitespace (e.g. U+200B) into source to dodge an accidental `*/` block-comment close — ESLint `no-irregular-whitespace` fails the lint gate. Reword the prose so the literal `*/` fence never appears (drop the inline example or describe it), rather than hiding a control byte in the comment.

shell-quoting-never-pipe-a-json-payload.rule: Never pipe a JSON payload through echo in zsh: zsh's echo turns \n escapes inside JSON strings into real newlines, the JSON becomes invalid, and a hook fed that way silently prints nothing, which looks like a product bug. Use printf '%s\n' "$payload" (or print -r --).

shell-quoting-rule-1.rule: For inline Node scripts that use top-level `await`, use ESM `import` syntax; otherwise wrap CommonJS `require` code in an async IIFE. Never mix `require` with top-level `await` in the same heredoc — Node 24 emits `ERR_AMBIGUOUS_MODULE_SYNTAX`.

shell-quoting-rule-10.rule: Installer scripts that auto-edit shell rc files must key BOTH the rc file path AND the line syntax off the shell name. `export PATH=...` is bash/POSIX-only — fish rejects it. For fish, use `fish_add_path -gP "$BIN_DIR"` (or `set -gx PATH "$BIN_DIR" $PATH`). Always `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$config")"` before `>>` because `~/.config/fish/` may not exist.

shell-quoting-rule-11.rule: When parsing structured `<token>  <filename>` manifests (checksums, etc.) from shell, use `awk -v t="$TARGET" '$2==t {print $1}'` — field equality, not `grep "$NEEDLE"` substring. Substring matching silently breaks when filenames share prefixes (e.g., `agentsmesh-darwin-arm64` vs `agentsmesh-darwin-arm64.exe`).

shell-quoting-rule-12.rule: Validate env-controlled paths (e.g., `$AGENTSMESH_INSTALL`) against a strict allowlist (`*[!a-zA-Z0-9./_~\ -]*`) before interpolating into any line written to a shell-rc file. Otherwise a wrapping process can inject persistent shell code via the env var.

shell-quoting-rule-13.rule: When a build/test fails with parser errors ("Unterminated string literal", "Unexpected `<<`"), scan touched files for unresolved `<<<<<<<` merge conflict markers FIRST before deeper investigation — higher-level debugging on a syntactically invalid file is noise.

shell-quoting-rule-14.rule: When an `rg` search pattern starts with `-` (or may start with `-` after interpolation), pass it with `-e '<pattern>'` or place `--` before the pattern so ripgrep cannot parse the search text as flags.

shell-quoting-rule-2.rule: Never put escaped newlines (`\n`) inside a plain `rg` regex; ripgrep is line-oriented by default. Split into multiple literal patterns, or pass `rg -U --multiline-dotall` when a true cross-line match is required.

shell-quoting-rule-3.rule: Never assign to `status` (or other zsh read-only specials) in shell cleanup snippets — use neutral names like `rc` for captured exit codes. Verify cleanup ran when the sandbox/wrapper exits unexpectedly.

shell-quoting-rule-4.rule: For `rg` patterns containing backticks, `$`, or other shell metacharacters, use single quotes with `-F` (literal mode), or split into simpler literal patterns. Never wrap such patterns in double quotes — the shell command-substitutes the backticks before `rg` ever runs.

shell-quoting-rule-5.rule: For `execSync`/`spawnSync` calls that need shell features like `2>&1`, use `/bin/sh` (or omit `shell` and avoid shell-only syntax). Never hardcode `/bin/zsh` (missing on `ubuntu-latest`) or `/bin/bash` (not guaranteed on minimal images) unless the job explicitly installs that shell.

shell-quoting-rule-6.rule: For tests that need merged stdout+stderr cross-platform, use `spawnSync(process.execPath, [...args], { encoding: 'utf-8' })` and concatenate `result.stdout + result.stderr`. Never embed `2>&1` or hardcode any `/bin/*` once Windows is in the CI matrix.

shell-quoting-rule-7.rule: Never write a literal `*/` inside any `/* ... */` or `/** ... */` block comment — including JSDoc headers in test files. Globs like `skills/*/SKILL.md` close the comment early and produce misleading parser errors at unrelated lines. Reword to `skills/{name}/SKILL.md`, `glob: *.md`, or move into a `//` single-line comment.

shell-quoting-rule-8.rule: When a TS/JS source file needs control-character escapes inside regex literals, build the regex via `new RegExp('[<>:"|?*\\u0000-\\u001F]')` or `String.fromCharCode(n)` — never put `\xNN`/`\uNNNN` directly in a `Write` tool payload, because JSON evaluates them into raw control bytes before the file is written. Verify the resulting file with `file(1)` is reported as text, not `data`.

shell-quoting-rule-9.rule: When a fixture string needs literal `<<<<<<< HEAD` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` lines at module top level, either (a) inline the literal inside a CallExpression argument, or (b) build it from concatenated parts (`'<' + '<<<<<< HEAD'`) so no source line begins with seven repeated `<`/`=`/`>`. TypeScript's lexer scans for left-anchored merge-conflict markers even inside top-level template literals (TS1185).

skill-path-resolution-resolve-skill-path.rule: Resolve skill paths from the declared skill roots before reading them.
Resolve skill paths from the repository-local skill root when a listed home-directory alias is absent.

source-verification-before-writing-or-ac.rule: Before writing or acting on a "submit this project to <list/registry>" step, check whether a submission from the same author is already open, and read the validator source (e.g. .github/workflows/validate-new-issue.yml) rather than only the CONTRIBUTING prose — awesome-claude-code checks one-open-submission-per-author BEFORE the age/stars gate and auto-closes duplicates, so a generic rejection message can mean "you already have one open", not "you were judged unworthy".

source-verification-keep-web-search-call.rule: Keep web search calls in functions.exec syntactically minimal; assign the query array to a variable before passing it to web__run when nested quoting has already caused a parser failure.

source-verification-re-open-official-doc.rule: Re-open official documentation from a fresh search result when a stale browser reference fails.

source-verification-when-a-validator-rep.rule: When a validator reports one error, do not assume it is the only one — check whether the checks are staged. awesome-claude-code parse_issue_form.py skips the sub-category check while the category is invalid, so fixing only the reported field surfaces a fresh failure on the next run. Read the validation source and fix every stale field in one edit.

stale-cleanup-do-not-pass-the-lock.rationale: The check caller and the generate caller need opposite set differences over the same map.
stale-cleanup-do-not-pass-the-lock.rule: Do not pass the lock's outputs map as both expectedPaths and provenance to findStaleGeneratedOutputs; lock-sync.ts already passes it as expectedPaths, so gating there makes outputsStale empty for every input and silently kills the check drift gate. Keep provenance an optional parameter that check omits.

stale-cleanup-never-delete-a-file-found.rationale: The sweep deleted Kiro-authored .kiro/hooks files, user-authored .claude/skills and Cursor-generated .cursor/rules on every generate.
stale-cleanup-never-delete-a-file-found.rule: Never delete a file found by the managedOutputs.dirs sweep without provenance from the previous run's lock outputs map; dirs are shared with the tools and users, and coOwnedFiles cannot cover them because their contents are dynamic.

subagent-delegation-in-workflow-scripts-.rationale: Two of four identical-schema explorers failed all 5 StructuredOutput retries and returned null, thinning the design-stage input; the null-tolerant digest was what kept the workflow usable.
subagent-delegation-in-workflow-scripts-.rule: In Workflow scripts, treat every agent() result as possibly null in downstream digests AND keep StructuredOutput schemas permissive for long-running analysts (few required fields, generous maxItems, no tight nested required arrays; consider a plain report:string fallback field) — strict schemas can burn the 5-retry StructuredOutput cap and silently null out an agent's entire multi-minute analysis.

subagent-delegation-never-relay-an-audit.rule: Never relay an audit subagent's "byte-identical / verified via diff" duplication claim without re-checking it yourself: in the pack-writer vs pack-merge audit the bodies were semantically identical but cosmetically different (a `dest` temp var, a differently-named dir const), which my normalized hash caught and the agent's diff claim did not. The distinction changes the fix — cosmetically-different twins parameterize into ONE helper, whereas truly identical ones just move to a shared module. Read both bodies before reporting.

subagent-delegation-validate-schema-d-su.rule: Validate schema'd subagent results for placeholder degeneracy before trusting them — a StructuredOutput schema guarantees shape, not content, and an agent can satisfy it with single-letter junk values (title 't', file 'f', scenario 's'). Spot-check at least one field of each result against reality; if degenerate, re-run that agent directly instead of counting the dimension as covered.

subagent-delegation-when-partitioning-co.rule: When partitioning consolidation/audit work across parallel agents by cluster, make the verifier check CROSS-cluster ownership before treating an in-cluster gap as a failure: content-twins without lineage links are often legitimately owned by a sibling cluster's output — resolve by looking up the sibling's replaces/leftovers list, and add a cross-cluster ownership note instead of duplicating the item in both clusters.

subagent-delegation-when-spawning-a-full.rule: When spawning a full-history subagent, omit agent_type/model/reasoning overrides; use a clean context if a specialized role is required.

target-capabilities-amp-has-no-documente.rationale: Independent re-verification for the amp/hooks capability-ledger finding directly contradicted an existing active lesson; primary-source check (live + 14mo of archives) wins over an unverifiable lesson citation.
target-capabilities-amp-has-no-documente.rule: Amp has NO documented settings-file hooks schema at all — ampcode.com/manual has never contained the word "hook" in its rendered text (verified via live full-page render AND 14+ months of Wayback Machine snapshots, May 2025 through Jul 2026, all zero matches; ampcode/amp-examples-and-guides repo has no hook-related files either). A prior lesson claimed a concrete `amp.hooks` array schema (compatibilityDate/tool:pre-execute/redact-tool-input) citing the bare manual URL with no quote — that was a hallucination (likely from an LLM web-search summarizer, not the actual page) and has been deprecated. Amp's only hook-like mechanism is the undocumented-in-manual `amp.on(...)` plugin API (code, not a declarative file). Declare amp hooks capability 'none' for both scopes; do not trust a ledger/lesson claim about a specific JSON schema without fetching and grep'ing the actual live (and if suspicious, archived) page text yourself.

target-capabilities-amp-s-real-amp-hooks.rule: Amp's real amp.hooks is a flat ARRAY of rule objects [{id, compatibilityDate, on:{event:'tool:pre-execute'|'tool:post-execute', tool:[...], 'input.contains':'...'}, action:{type:'send-user-message'|'redact-tool-input', message:'...'}}] read from .amp/settings.json and ~/.config/amp/settings.json; agentsmesh emits a Claude-Code-shaped OBJECT keyed by event ({event:[{matcher,hooks:[{type,command}]}]}) under amp.hooks and has NO hooks importer, so the round-trip is broken. Do not declare amp hooks 'native' — it is 'embedded' at best until the emitter matches Amp's array schema and an importer exists.

target-capabilities-an-amazon-q-custom-a.rationale: crates/chat-cli/src/cli/agent/mod.rs: `Agent::default()` injects RULES_PATTERN, but `#[serde(default)]` on the `resources` field means a parsed custom agent starts empty.
target-capabilities-an-amazon-q-custom-a.rule: An Amazon Q custom agent JSON deserializes `resources` with serde default (empty), so it does NOT inherit the built-in default agent's `.amazonq/rules/**/*.md` glob — always write the rules glob into every generated agent JSON or the generated rules are never loaded for anyone who selects that agent.

target-capabilities-copilot-has-no-globa.rationale: Global commands declared native but Copilot CLI never reads ~/.copilot/prompts; output is silently inert.
target-capabilities-copilot-has-no-globa.rule: Copilot has NO global ~/.copilot/prompts/ surface: the official ~/.copilot config-dir reference enumerates all top-level items (agents, skills, hooks, instructions, copilot-instructions.md) and lists no prompts dir; .prompt.md is a VS Code/IDE feature. Do not declare global commands:native for copilot or emit .copilot/prompts/*.prompt.md — it is a phantom (inert) path.

target-capabilities-deepagents-cli-hooks.rule: deepagents-cli hooks are NOT Claude Code format: Deep Agents Code reads hooks.json as {\"hooks\":[{\"command\":[...],\"events\":[\"session.start\",\"session.end\",\"tool.error\",...]}]} (array of command+events objects), not the PreToolUse/PostToolUse matcher object buildClaudeHooksObjectFromCanonical emits; the generator emits the wrong schema and there is no hooks importer, so hooks:native is generate-only and produces an invalid file. Emit the deepagents array schema and wire a hooks importer.

target-capabilities-deepagents-cli-targe.rule: deepagents-cli target wraps LangChain "Deep Agents Code" (libs/code/deepagents_code), which loads custom subagents from the filesystem as Markdown+YAML-frontmatter at .deepagents/agents/{name}/AGENTS.md (project) and ~/.deepagents/{agent}/agents/{name}/AGENTS.md (user); declare agents as native, not none.

target-capabilities-for-amazon-q-global-.rationale: paths.rs `mod global` has no rules constant, so `.aws/amazonq/rules/*.md` was dead until an agent JSON pointed at it; the agent `resources` array is the mechanism that actually works.
target-capabilities-for-amazon-q-global-.rule: For amazon-q global scope, do not treat "Q CLI has no global rules directory" as "global rules are impossible": route global rules and additionalRules through the generated agent JSON `resources` array as `file://~/.aws/amazonq/rules/**/*.md` (collect_resources runs shellexpand, so `~` expands), and declare both capabilities `embedded`, not `none` or `native`.

target-capabilities-for-kilo-code-the-ne.rule: For kilo-code, the new-layout `.kilo/rules/*.md` files are NOT auto-loaded by Kilo Code — each must be registered under the `instructions` array in `kilo.jsonc` (only legacy `.kilocode/rules/` auto-loads). Generating standalone `.kilo/rules/<slug>.md` without writing an `instructions` entry leaves additionalRules silently inert. Also: kilo global commands/agents live at `~/.config/kilo/commands|agents` (NOT `~/.kilo/`), global skills live at `~/.kilo/skills`, and MCP belongs in `kilo.jsonc` top-level `mcp` key (not `.kilo/mcp.json` `mcpServers`).

target-capabilities-for-opencode-ignore-.rationale: Verified against the live schema (opencode.ai/config.json, Config.additionalProperties=false) and opencode.ai/docs/permissions.
target-capabilities-for-opencode-ignore-.rule: For opencode ignore, map canonical patterns onto permission.read/permission.edit path deny rules — never watcher.ignore (watcher-only, does not block reads) and never grep/glob (their rules match the search string, not the file path). Emit deny rules only: user rules append AFTER OpenCode's built-in defaults with last-match-wins, so a generated "*": "allow" catch-all silently undoes OpenCode's own .env protection.

target-capabilities-for-the-crush-target.rule: For the crush target, only emit permissions.allowed_tools in crush.json — Crush's Go Permissions struct has no denied_tools field (json:"allowed_tools" only), so generated denied_tools is silently ignored; also permissions is a real on-disk crush.json key (read from project crush.json and global ~/.config/crush/crush.json), so it must be declared native, not partial/none.

target-capabilities-when-a-target-s-perm.rationale: Escaping silently disabled a user's own deny rule on the documented import --global -> generate --global path.
target-capabilities-when-a-target-s-perm.rule: When a target's permission surface stores REGEX patterns (Warp `[agents.profiles]` command lists), never regex-escape the canonical `Bash(<payload>)` payload on generate — an imported user regex like `rm -rf .*` comes back as `rm \-rf \.\*` and stops matching. Pass the payload through verbatim, anchor allowlist entries (`^…$`) and leave denylist entries unanchored, so each list takes the narrower reading of the undocumented match semantics.

target-capabilities-when-auditing-the-an.rule: When auditing the antigravity target's permissions capability, treat the official allowlist-denylist/permissions docs (Allow/Ask/Deny, app-managed project permissions) as the source of truth; only third-party blogs claim a committable .antigravity/settings.json with antigravity.commands.alwaysAllow/alwaysDeny keys, so cap any permissions upgrade at embedded with explicit low/medium confidence rather than native.

target-capabilities-when-declaring-the-c.rule: When declaring the copilot hooks capability, use 'native' (not 'partial') for project scope: Copilot CLI auto-loads .github/hooks/*.json at startup and agentsmesh fully owns/round-trips .github/hooks/agentsmesh.json. Global hooks are also native via ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json (same JSON format).

target-capabilities-when-one-generated-a.rationale: config.features filters which generators run, never which keys a shared artifact contains.
target-capabilities-when-one-generated-a.rule: When one generated artifact carries several canonical features (e.g. an Amazon Q agent JSON holding agents+hooks+permissions+ignore), gate every embedded key on the enabled feature set inside the descriptor's `emitScopedSettings` hook — feature generators receive only `{capability, scope}`, so a builder that reads `canonical.ignore`/`hooks`/`permissions` directly leaks features the user disabled in `agentsmesh.yaml`.

target-capability-audits-a-test-fixture-.rule: A test fixture placed under a path the repo .gitignores (e.g. tests/e2e/fixtures/<x>/.cursor/, .github/hooks/) is SILENTLY dropped by `git add` (the gitignore no-op), so it never reaches CI while existing on your disk. Signature: a fixture-reading test passes locally but fails on CI with "Expected file to exist" or missing-derived-output (e.g. cursor import producing no .agentsmesh/hooks.yaml). Fix: `git add -f <fixture>` and confirm with `git ls-files <fixture>`. When adding any fixture file, check `git check-ignore -v <path>` first; sibling fixtures may be tracked from a prior force-add while your new one is blocked.

target-capability-audits-after-changing-.rule: After changing a target's importFrom/importer logic, rebuild dist (pnpm build) BEFORE running the e2e round-trip matrix: tests/e2e/target-contract-matrix.e2e.test.ts spawns the built dist/cli.js via runCli, while tests/contract/target-contract.matrix.test.ts calls importFrom in-process. If the contract round-trip passes but the e2e round-trip fails with a missing/extra canonical file (e.g. .agentsmesh/hooks.yaml), the dist is stale — rebuild, don't chase the importer.

target-capability-audits-augment-code-to.rule: Augment Code tool permissions are GLOBAL/CLI-only: `toolPermissions` lives in the personal `~/.augment/settings.json` ([{toolName, permission:{type: allow|deny|ask-user}}], maps to canonical allow/deny/ask) and per docs.augmentcode.com/cli/permissions applies only in the Auggie CLI, NOT the IDE extension and NOT project `.augment/settings.json`. So raise permissions to native for GLOBAL scope only (gate it in buildSettingsContent on scope==='global' and import on scope==='global'); project stays none. General rule: confirm a capability's real scope from the tool's own docs, not from agentsmesh's own code comments — an internal comment claiming a key exists is not primary-source verification.

target-capability-audits-augment-code-to.rationale: The prior lesson asserted project scope must stay none, which contradicted Augment's own docs and would have blocked a real capability.
target-capability-audits-augment-code-to.rule: Augment Code `toolPermissions` is native at BOTH scopes, not global-only. docs.augmentcode.com/cli/permissions documents two settings files with the same shape: `~/.augment/settings.json` (user) and `.augment/settings.json` described as "Repo-level settings committed to the project, applied to any agent running in that repo" — committing it is the documented way to enforce org policy. Entries are `{toolName, permission:{type: allow|deny|ask-user}}`, honored by the Auggie CLI and Cosmos cloud agents but not the IDE extension. Do not gate emission or import on `scope === 'global'`.

target-capability-audits-capability-audi.rule: Capability audits for agentsmesh are expansion-first: preserve working experimental, compatibility, and unofficial target projections; do not downgrade or remove support merely because the vendor surface is experimental or not the preferred path. Add newly available features and document limitations.

target-capability-audits-cline-has-no-gl.rule: Cline has NO global agent-definition surface: the official ~/.cline/ tree is data/settings/{providers.json,rules/,skills/}, data/teams/, data/sessions/, data/logs/, plugins/ — no agents.yaml and no agents/ dir. agents.yaml exists ONLY at project .cline/agents.yaml (single YAML file, not a .cline/agents/*.md directory). Do not declare cline globalCapabilities.agents as 'native' and do not emit global ~/.cline/agents/*.md; global agents support is effectively none.

target-capability-audits-continue-agent-.rationale: The prior lesson claimed a project-.md / global-.yaml split; reading ConfigHandler.getLocalProfiles, getDotContinueSubDirs and AgentFileService shows both scopes behave identically.
target-capability-audits-continue-agent-.rule: Continue agent files are `.continue/agents/<name>.md` at BOTH scopes — the format does not vary by scope. `getDotContinueSubDirs` adds `~/.continue/<subdir>` to the same scan under `includeGlobal`, so the `fileExtType: 'yaml'` agents scan in `ConfigHandler.getLocalProfiles` treats YAML there as an *assistant profile* at every scope; markdown agent files are loaded by explicit path via `AgentFileService.getAgentFile` -> `path.resolve`, which is location-independent. Never emit, import, or stale-delete `.continue/agents/*.yaml`.

target-capability-audits-continue-hooks-.rationale: A prior lesson declared Continue hooks unsupported based on config.yaml's schema only; the CLI reads hooks from settings.json, so the earlier audit under-reported two capabilities.
target-capability-audits-continue-hooks-.rule: Continue hooks ARE native at both scopes: they live under the `hooks` key of `.continue/settings.json` / `~/.continue/settings.json` (Claude-Code-compatible shape, 17 events), NOT in config.yaml — verify extensions/cli/src/hooks/hookConfig.ts before concluding a Continue feature is unsupported from config.yaml alone. Continue agents are native too but the format differs by scope: `.continue/agents/<name>.md` (markdown agent file, `tools` must be a comma STRING) at project, `.continue/agents/<name>.yaml` (assistant profile) at global.

Continue hooks are native at both scopes: they live under the `hooks` key of `.continue/settings.json` / `~/.continue/settings.json` in the Claude-Code-compatible shape (17 events), NOT in config.yaml — check extensions/cli/src/hooks/hookConfig.ts before concluding a Continue feature is unsupported from config.yaml alone.

target-capability-audits-cursor-ide-perm.rule: Cursor IDE permissions are file-based and disk-ownable via .cursor/permissions.json (project) and ~/.cursor/permissions.json (global), JSONC, top-level keys mcpAllowlist/terminalAllowlist/autoRun{allow_instructions,block_instructions} — NOT GUI-only, so 'partial'/'none' under-declares; but canonical allow/deny/ask does not round-trip losslessly (no enforceable deny/ask, allow must be split terminal-vs-MCP). The legacy importer's .cursor/settings.json permissions key is an undocumented phantom path; the real file is .cursor/permissions.json.

target-capability-audits-for-a-global-on.rule: For a GLOBAL-ONLY settings-backed capability (permissions/mcp/hooks/ignore native at global but none at project), generate via globalSupport.scopeExtras (scope-aware), NOT a plain generators.generateX. The engine's generatePermissionsFeature calls gen(canonical) with no scope, and resolveTargetFeatureGenerator returns the generator regardless of capability level, so a generateX would leak the file into project scope. The descriptor schema's validateCapabilityImplementations accepts globalSupport.scopeExtras as a valid implementation for settings-backed features at global scope only.

target-capability-audits-for-codex-cli-c.rule: For codex-cli, `.codex/instructions/<slug>.md` is NOT a surface Codex reads (config reference marks `instructions` as reserved/future-use); Codex's real additional-rule surfaces are nested `AGENTS.md`/`AGENTS.override.md` (advisory) and `.codex/rules/*.rules` (execution policy, Starlark prefix_rule). Do not treat the instructions-mirror emit as a native additionalRules surface. Also: codex MCP `.codex/config.toml` natively supports streamable-HTTP servers via `url`/`bearer_token_env_var`/`http_headers`/`env_http_headers` (not experimental), and that file is Codex's primary config — generateMcp overwriting it whole drops both HTTP servers and all non-MCP user config.

target-capability-audits-for-gemini-cli-.rule: For Gemini CLI permissions, global (User-tier ~/.gemini/policies/*.toml) is fully loaded by the policy engine and is the recommended location, but project/workspace-tier ($WORKSPACE_ROOT/.gemini/policies/*.toml) is temporarily DISABLED upstream (issue #18186, PR #20522). So gemini-cli global permissions should be 'native' while project stays 'partial'; never raise the project permissions level above partial.

target-capability-audits-for-qwen-code-g.rule: For qwen-code, global additionalRules is native, not embedded: Qwen Code auto-loads ~/.qwen/rules/**/*.md (md + optional YAML frontmatter with description/paths) globally per PR #3339 (merged 2026-04-17), mirroring project .qwen/rules/. Wire a global rules dir constant + global layout rewrite + importer-spec global source instead of embedding into ~/.qwen/QWEN.md.

target-capability-audits-for-the-continu.rule: For the Continue target, permissions live ONLY in the global ~/.continue/permissions.yaml (Continue CLI surface, top-level keys allow/ask/exclude) — there is NO project-level permissions file; raise permissions capability for global scope only, keep project permissions=none. Hooks are NOT in Continue's config.yaml schema (verified against docs/reference and config_schema.json), so hooks must stay none for both scopes.

target-capability-audits-goose-supports-.rule: Goose supports file-based tool permissions natively in GLOBAL scope only via ~/.config/goose/permission.yaml — a YAML map keyed by category (user, smart_approve) where each category has always_allow/ask_before/never_allow string lists (verified in crates/goose/src/config/permission.rs). agentsmesh owns the `user` block (allow→always_allow, deny→never_allow, ask→ask_before) and MUST merge-preserve the runtime `smart_approve` cache. There is NO project-level permission.yaml, so project permissions stays 'none'. MCP and permissions are both global-only for Goose.

Goose supports lifecycle hooks via the Open Plugin Specification v1.0.0: a `hooks/hooks.json` file inside a plugin dir at `<project>/.agents/plugins/<name>/` (project scope) and `~/.agents/plugins/<name>/` (global scope), auto-discovered at startup (released 2026-05-14). Schema: top-level `hooks` object keyed by event (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure/SessionStart/SessionEnd/UserPromptSubmit/...), each an array of `{matcher?, hooks:[{type:"command", command}]}`. This maps onto canonical Hooks (event -> HookEntry{matcher,command,type}), so hooks is UNDER-declared as 'none' for both scopes; both project and global are file-based and round-trippable. Note the plugin-dir nesting (agentsmesh must own a plugin <name> dir), unlike Claude Code's single settings hooks key.

target-capability-audits-in-capability-l.rationale: Blanking a path to record a "none" doc verdict broke conformance for goose/ignore and rovodev/hooks; the two axes are independent.
target-capability-audits-in-capability-l.rule: In capability-ledger.json, a cell whose DESCRIPTOR level is native/embedded must carry path/ext/format/fingerprint derived from the actual generated output (probe it with a tsx script over tests/e2e/fixtures/canonical-full), not from the tool's docs — the conformance test validates by descriptor level, so a doc-derived path fails with "no result emitted at path". Record the documentation verdict in maxAchievable/verdict/rejectionReason instead; the audit then surfaces the mismatch as `over-declared`.

target-capability-audits-keep-capability.rule: Keep capability-audit inspection commands limited to real repository modules; do not append placeholder require probes after a successful audit because they turn a valid audit run into a false command failure.

target-capability-audits-never-list-a-na.rationale: Continue's `.continue/agents` held user assistant profiles that generate deleted.
target-capability-audits-never-list-a-na.rule: Never list a native directory in `TargetLayout.managedOutputs.dirs` when the tool also stores user-authored artifacts there: `cleanupStaleGeneratedOutputs` deletes every file in a managed dir the current generate run did not emit, so hand-written config is destroyed outright. Prefer losing stale-file eviction over deleting user files.

target-capability-audits-pi-pi-agent-nat.rule: Pi (pi-agent) natively supports prompt templates as command surface: project `.pi/prompts/*.md` and global `~/.pi/agent/prompts/*.md` (non-recursive, filename = command name, YAML frontmatter `description` + `argument-hint`, `$1`/`$ARGUMENTS` substitution). Treat `commands` as a native, round-trippable file surface — do not leave it declared `none` while only projecting commands as `.pi/skills/` bundles via supportsConversion.

target-capability-audits-when-a-capabili.rule: When a capability finding's cited source URL, once fetched, does not mention the claimed feature at all (e.g. 'prompts.yml' absent from manage-rovo-dev-cli-settings/), do not conclude the finding is fabricated yet — check sibling pages on the same docs site (via its nav/TOC, e.g. a linked 'Save and reuse a prompt' page) before rejecting. A miscited URL is common; the real primary-source proof and a 'no global surface' claim can both be one click away and directly contradict the given instruction.

target-capability-audits-when-a-generato.rationale: A scope branch to a distinct filename is unverifiable from the descriptor alone and produces artifacts no tool reads; tests passed because they asserted our own output.
target-capability-audits-when-a-generato.rule: When a generator branches on scope to a DIFFERENT output path (e.g. `if (ctx?.scope === 'global') return [{ path: SOME_OTHER_FILE }]`), verify that global path against the tool's own docs before trusting it — this branch is where fabricated surfaces hide. Claude Code's global hooks were written to `~/.claude/hooks.json`, a file its docs never list (hooks belong in `~/.claude/settings.json` under `hooks`), so global hooks silently never loaded. Same class: gemini-cli project `.gemini/policies/`, goose `.gooseignore`.

target-capability-audits-when-a-target-d.rationale: codex-cli declared hooks=partial yet had generateHooks + importCodexHooks + round-trip tests + managedOutputs; partial was wrong, native was correct.
target-capability-audits-when-a-target-d.rule: When a target declares a feature `partial` but already ships a REAL generator AND importer for it (a dedicated on-disk file the tool reads, round-trip tested) — not a no-op stub — the level is a mislabel: raise it to `native`. `partial` is reserved for features that have only a no-op `generateX` returning [] plus a `lint.<feature>` warning (GUI/cloud-only surfaces agentsmesh cannot write). Diagnostic: a `partial` feature with no `lint.<feature>` stub and a wired generator in `target.generators` is almost certainly mislabeled.

target-capability-audits-when-a-target-d.rationale: Capability levels are metadata; only rewriteGeneratedPath (or a scope-aware generator) actually suppresses an output at global scope.
target-capability-audits-when-a-target-d.rule: When a target declares a global capability as `none` or `partial`, verify `globalSupport.layout.rewriteGeneratedPath` returns null for that feature's project path — the generate engine never gates generators on capability level, so a project-shaped output silently lands at the home root (warp emitted a bare ~/AGENTS.md while globalCapabilities.rules was 'none').

target-capability-audits-when-a-target-d.rationale: replit-agent shipped commands/agents at `none` while emitting both to .agents/skills; the gap was pure declaration drift.
target-capability-audits-when-a-target-d.rule: When a target descriptor declares `commands`/`agents` as `none` but also sets `supportsConversion` plus a wired `generateCommands`/`generateAgents`, the generate engine already emits those skill bundles — the level is a mislabel, not a missing feature. Probe with a real `generate()` test before writing generator code, then fix the capability to `embedded` and add the matching `conversionDefaults` so `usesCommandSkillProjection`/`usesAgentSkillProjection` agree with the dispatcher.

target-capability-audits-when-a-target-g.rule: When a target gains a NEW generated managed-output file (added to layout.managedOutputs.files), update TWO exact-file-set assertions, not just one: the target's contract (tests/contract/contracts/<id>.ts generated[]) AND its per-target dirTreeExactly assertion in tests/e2e/generate-capabilities.e2e.test.ts. The contract round-trip test passing in-process does not cover the e2e dirTreeExactly, which spawns the built CLI and lists every file — so a new file (e.g. .aider.conf.yml) fails there with an exact-tree mismatch until you add it (in sorted order) to both lists.

target-capability-audits-when-changing-a.rationale: Cursor hooks format fix (PascalCase nested -> camelCase flat) broke 9 cross-cutting test files beyond the cursor unit dir.
target-capability-audits-when-changing-a.rule: When changing a target's generated FILE FORMAT (hook event names, object shape, or top-level key — not just the path), grep the ENTIRE tests/ tree before claiming the slice done, not just tests/unit/targets/<id>/. Format changes have wide blast radius: cross-cutting fixtures and assertions live in tests/unit/core/engine.test.ts, tests/import-generate-roundtrip.test.ts, tests/integration/*-merge & generate.integration, tests/e2e/{import,generate}-capabilities, global-roundtrip-*, hooks-roundtrip, and tests/e2e/fixtures/<target>-project/. Update every one in the same TDD slice.

When changing a target's command/agent/skill/root native OUTPUT path (e.g. command projection→native), update BOTH ternary chains in tests/e2e/helpers/reference-targets.ts: outputPaths() AND expectedRefs(). The generate/round-trip matrix test reads expectedRefs(target).command for its expectAnyPathTail assertions, so editing only outputPaths leaves the test asserting the stale path and it fails with "expected <new body> to contain <old path tail>".

target-capability-audits-when-dozens-of-.rule: When dozens of CLI renderer / logger color tests fail LOCALLY (e.g. "respects NO_COLOR env", check/generate/install/lint renderers) but CI is green, suspect FORCE_COLOR in your shell, not a regression. The harness sets FORCE_COLOR=3; FORCE_COLOR overrides NO_COLOR, so tests that assert no-ANSI output while only clearing NO_COLOR (not FORCE_COLOR) emit color and fail. Confirm with `node -e "console.log(process.env.FORCE_COLOR)"`; run/commit with `env -u FORCE_COLOR <cmd>` so the pre-commit hook's suite (and these tests) pass. This also explains a pre-commit hook that fails locally on a markdown-only commit.

target-capability-audits-when-extracting.rule: When extracting capabilities to a separate file to stay under the 200-line limit, export named constants (e.g. `projectCapabilities`, `globalCapabilities`) rather than the same names as the inline variables in index.ts — this avoids name shadowing and import confusion when the old variables are removed.

target-capability-expansion-amazon-q-cli.rule: Amazon Q CLI reads rules ONLY from project .amazonq/rules/**/*.md (auto-loaded directory of multiple .md files); it has NO global rules dir on disk (open feature request aws/amazon-q-developer-cli#3451 asks for ~/.amazonq/rules, not ~/.aws/amazonq/rules). Keep amazon-q additionalRules native for PROJECT but none for GLOBAL; the ~/.aws/amazonq/ root is real only for MCP/agents.

target-capability-expansion-before-readi.rule: Before reading a target implementation, list its files or search for the symbol; do not assume split generator/importer filenames because many targets keep them in aggregate files.

target-capability-expansion-conversion-d.rule: Conversion-disable flags must suppress only conversion-derived embedded generators; once a target gains native support, conversion settings must not disable its native generator.

target-capability-expansion-do-not-combi.rule: Do not combine an expected no-match rg probe after another read command when failure capture is mandatory; run no-match-tolerant searches separately or use an explicit read-only fallback.

target-capability-expansion-for-opencode.rule: For opencode targets, additionalRules emitted to .opencode/rules/ are NOT auto-loaded by opencode (only AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md are); to make additionalRules genuinely native, the generator must also write an "instructions" array (e.g. [".opencode/rules/*.md"]) into opencode.json, otherwise the rule files are orphaned and additionalRules is over-declared as native.

target-capability-expansion-native-targe.rule: Native target agent formats that omit canonical fields must carry those fields in x-agentsmesh extension metadata, and their import mapper must explicitly translate the extensions back before fallback serialization.

target-capability-expansion-repo-wide-pr.rationale: Every remaining target-fix task in this campaign will hit the same pre-existing repo-wide coverage gate; know it's not yours to fix before spending hours chasing it.
target-capability-expansion-repo-wide-pr.rule: Repo-wide pre-commit hook (.husky/pre-commit -> pnpm precommit) runs pnpm test:coverage with a 95% global branch threshold; this is separate from and stricter than the task's own pnpm test gate. Verified via coverage/coverage-final.json branch counts that a ~21-branch (0.18%) shortfall is spread across many pre-existing files unrelated to any single target fix (roo-code importer/layout/merge, windsurf hooks/rules/skills, utils/logger, utils/text/markdown) — not something one target's capability fix can or should close. Do not skip hooks without explicit user authorization; report the blocker instead of committing.

target-capability-expansion-when-a-targe.rule: When a target gains support for a previously linted unsupported feature, remove or rewrite branch tests for the obsolete lint helper in the same capability slice.
When a target output family changes, update shared E2E manifest helpers and reference-matrix expectations in addition to generation assertions; these helpers may encode the old path independently.

target-capability-expansion-when-adding-.rule: When adding a new settings-backed feature (e.g. permissions) to a directory a target already uses for per-rule/slug-derived filenames (e.g. codex-cli's .codex/rules/{slug}.rules execution rules), pick a dedicated filename distinct from both the slug pattern AND the tool's own well-known write destination (e.g. Codex TUI writes to default.rules) — verify against real e2e fixtures for plausible user-authored slugs that could collide (a rule literally named default.md already exists in tests/e2e/codex-format-roundtrip.e2e.test.ts) before choosing a name.

target-capability-expansion-when-expandi.rule: When expanding a target from agent-to-skill projection to native agent files, update strict path contracts and preserve canonical-only metadata in extension frontmatter so generate-import round trips remain lossless.

target-capability-expansion-when-repo-wi.rule: When repo-wide format:check reports pre-existing drift, format only touched files and recheck that subset; do not rewrite unrelated source files.

target-deepagents-cli-deepagents-cli-glo.rule: deepagents-cli globals are per-agent: user memory is ~/.deepagents/{assistant_id}/AGENTS.md and user skills are ~/.deepagents/{assistant_id}/skills/ (NOT flat ~/.deepagents/AGENTS.md or ~/.deepagents/skills). Its hooks.json is {"hooks":[{"command":[..],"events":["session.start"]}]} loaded only from ~/.deepagents/hooks.json — NOT the Claude-Code PreToolUse/matcher object shape, and there is no project hooks surface. deepagents also has native on-disk agents dirs (.deepagents/agents/{name}/AGENTS.md project, ~/.deepagents/{agent}/agents/{name}/AGENTS.md global).

target-permissions-a-target-importer-mus.rationale: `rules: []` (the file agentsmesh itself writes on revocation) imported back and cleared canonical allow AND deny, silently dropping a protective Read(./.env) deny for claude-code and cursor.
target-permissions-a-target-importer-mus.rule: A target importer must never treat an empty or partial target-side list as a revocation of canonical: skip the write when the target yields no entries, and rewrite only the canonical lists (allow/deny/ask) the target actually carries entries for — canonical is shared, so a wipe leaks into every other target.

target-permissions-when-a-per-target-imp.rationale: A round-trip fixed-point test caught allow/deny/ask cross-contamination that per-entry unit tests did not.
target-permissions-when-a-per-target-imp.rule: When a per-target import fans one target file set into one canonical file (e.g. permissions from many agent profiles), filter imported records by their effect/list INSIDE the merge helper, not at the call site — passing the whole record set to each list merge silently duplicates every entry into allow, deny and ask.

target-permissions-when-a-target-generat.rationale: Whole-key replacement of `rules:` in ~/.kiro/settings/permissions.yaml deleted hand-written exclude protections, and a parse-error fallback to an empty Document deleted the whole file.
target-permissions-when-a-target-generat.rule: When a target generator rewrites a shared config file the user also edits, own it PER ELEMENT by shape (rewrite only the entries the generator itself emits, preserve everything else verbatim) and never fall back to a fresh document when the existing file fails to parse — return "no write" instead.

targets-a-target-declaring-additionalrul.rule: A target declaring `additionalRules: 'embedded'` MUST call `splitEmbeddedRulesToCanonical` in its importer. The descriptor `singleFile` runner copies the whole body — managed block included — into `_root.md`, and the next `generateRules` strips that block before rebuilding it, so every non-root rule is deleted on the documented generate -> import -> generate path.

targets-codex-marketplace-catalogs-rejec.rule: Codex marketplace catalogs reject `policy.authentication: "NONE"` — the only variants are ON_INSTALL and ON_USE, and the field is optional, so omit it for a plugin that authenticates nothing. Validate a catalog by actually running `codex plugin marketplace add <path>`; JSON-schema checks and `claude plugin validate` both pass a catalog Codex refuses. Verify a plugin end to end in an isolated CODEX_HOME=$(mktemp -d): `codex mcp list` there shows only the plugin-contributed server, and `codex exec` lists the bundled skill namespaced as `<plugin>:<skill>`.

targets-gemini-cli-hook-matchers-are.rule: Gemini CLI hook matchers are unanchored regexes over Gemini's own tool names: translate canonical matchers (Edit|Write|Bash) to Gemini tool names, never copy them verbatim.

targets-import-into-a-shared-canonical.rule: Import into a SHARED canonical file (`.agentsmesh/ignore`, `.agentsmesh/permissions.yaml`) must be additive. A native config is routinely only partly populated, so treating its silence as a deletion strips entries every other target relies on. Only a target-owned generated file may be treated as authoritative on import.

targets-in-a-target-unit-test.rationale: Cost 20 minutes debugging a commandPath returning null only in the descriptor unit test while real generate worked.
targets-in-a-target-unit-test.rule: In a target unit test, import `src/targets/catalog/builtin-targets.js` before the target's own `index.js`: entering the circular graph from the target module leaves that target's slot in BUILTIN_TARGETS undefined, so `getDescriptor(id)` returns undefined and `shouldConvertCommandsToSkills` silently falls back to false (commandPath returns null).

targets-never-invent-a-stricter-validato.rationale: kimi-code's permission-pattern regex rejected mcp__github__*, * and Tool(), all of which Kimi Code's parsePattern accepts, silently un-enforcing deny rules.
targets-never-invent-a-stricter-validato.rule: Never invent a stricter validator than the tool's own parser: copy the tool's parse function's exact accept/reject set (globs, wildcards, empty payloads), or valid user rules are silently dropped and the lint message states a false rule.

targets-never-list-a-tool-s.rationale: Found pre-existing in zed: .zed/settings.json was in managedOutputs.files while only being emitted when canonical had MCP servers.
targets-never-list-a-tool-s.rule: Never list a tool's general settings file (`.zed/settings.json`, `~/.config/zed/settings.json`, `~/.warp/settings.toml`) in `managedOutputs.files`: `cleanupStaleGeneratedOutputs` deletes every managed file a run did not emit, so one generate with no MCP servers wipes the user's whole editor config. Revoke inside the file with a key-scoped overlay instead.

targets-recall-hook-projection-happens-o.rule: Recall-hook projection happens only in the engine (withTargetRecallHooks in src/targets/catalog/recall-hook-targets.ts, applied to generate, postProcess, emitScopedSettings and scopeExtras). Target hook generators receive hooks that are already projected, so a unit test that calls a builtin hooks generator directly must pass withTargetRecallHooks(canonical, '<id>'), and must import the catalog before the target index.js to dodge the BUILTIN_TARGETS cycle.

targets-the-plugin-bundle-serves-two.rule: The plugin bundle serves two clients from one directory: Codex reads the portable Agent Plugins pair `plugin.json` + `mcp.json` at the bundle root (schemas at agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0, both set additionalProperties:false, so presentation must nest under `extensions.com.openai`), Claude Code reads `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `.mcp.json`. Keep ONE `skills/` copy. Marketplace catalogs live at repo root — `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` — and both resolve `./plugins/<name>` from the REPO root, not from the catalog directory (verified against openai/plugins). `claude plugin validate . --strict` additionally rejects a catalog with no top-level `description`, which the documented schema does not list as required.

targets-to-prove-a-claude-code.rationale: Tool presence is ambiguous when the user already configures a server of the same name; the plugin_ prefix is the only reliable attribution.
targets-to-prove-a-claude-code.rule: To prove a Claude Code plugin actually loaded, check the tool namespace, not just `claude plugin details`: plugin-provided MCP tools appear as `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__*`, which is distinct from a same-named server in the user's own config (`mcp__<server>__*`). Both can be present at once, so tool existence alone proves nothing. The bundled skill likewise appears namespaced as `<plugin>:<skill>`. Note plugins load at session start, so install then start a NEW session before looking.

targets-when-a-target-reads-several.rationale: kimi-code was built on a docs-only reading that the two AGENTS.md paths were alternatives; loadAgentsMdForRoots concatenates them, so import dropped a whole file and import->generate duplicated the rules.
targets-when-a-target-reads-several.rule: When a target reads several instruction files, verify from the tool's own loader source whether it CONCATENATES them or picks the first; if it concatenates, import every readable source and list the files generation does not write in managedOutputs so a leftover copy cannot double the rules in the prompt.

targets-when-a-target-writes-an.rationale: Codebuff's mcpConfigSchema is a z.strictObject union; loadMCPConfig `continue`s on parse failure, dropping every server in the file.
targets-when-a-target-writes-an.rule: When a target writes an MCP/config JSON file, validate the generated shape against the tool's ACTUAL parse schema from source (not just the file wrapper): strict/closed schemas reject the WHOLE file on one unknown key, so passing canonical `description`/`env` through silently disables every server.

targets-when-a-target-writes-keys.rationale: features default to every VALID_FEATURES entry, so an unconditional claim fires for everyone.
targets-when-a-target-writes-keys.rule: When a target writes keys into a file the USER owns (editor settings.json, config.toml), claim a key only when that feature's canonical SOURCE exists — `canonical.mcp === null` / `canonical.permissions === null` means "no opinion" while an empty-but-present file means "explicitly empty". Claiming unconditionally makes a plain `agentsmesh generate` delete hand-written config in any repo that has no `.agentsmesh/mcp.json` or `permissions.yaml`.

targets-when-importing-a-target-surface.rationale: Same failure class as the Warp allowlist escaping lesson, solved generically with a re-encode guard in zed permissions-map fromZedRule.
targets-when-importing-a-target-surface.rule: When importing a target surface that stores REGEXES back into canonical literals, only accept a value that re-encodes byte-for-byte through the generate mapping; otherwise a hand-written regex (`^cargo\s+(build|test)$`) decodes to a nonsense literal and the next generate escapes it into a pattern that matches nothing, silently disabling the user's own rule.

targets-when-merging-generated-entries-i.rule: When merging generated entries into a list inside a user-owned file, revoke ONLY entries the importer can decode back to canonical; entries it refuses (hand-written regexes, foreign shapes) are the user's and must survive every generate. Whole-list replace on an "owned" key silently deletes the user's own deny rules.

targets-when-two-targets-emit-into.rationale: Zed projecting commands into codex-cli's .agents/skills/ with an extra frontmatter key would have crashed every zed+codex-cli generate run.
